ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r2.claim: Shiqāʾ means hardship and badness of life, opposite saʿāda; the two forms may be transitive, as shown by the readings with ḍamma and lexicographic reports.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r2.anchor: الشقاء نكد العيش. وسوؤه. يقال منه: شقى يشقى شقاء وشقوة وشقاوة والسعادة ضده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Hudhayl use سعده الله with the meaning أسعده الله.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r3.anchor: وذكر أن الفراء حكى أن هذيلا تقول: سعده الله بمعنى أسعده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r4.speaker: الجوهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r4.claim: Al-Jawharī distinguishes سعد بالكسر فهو سعيد from سعد فهو مسعود, by analogy with سلم فهو سليم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r4.anchor: وقال الجوهري: سعد بالكسر فهو سعيد، مثل سلم فهو سليم، وسعد فهو مسعود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r5.speaker: أبو نصر عبد الرحيم القشيري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r5.claim: Abū Naṣr al-Qushayrī says سعده الله yields مسعود, while أسعده الله yields مسعد.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r5.anchor: وقال أبو نصر عبد الرحيم القشيري: ورد سعده الله فهو مسعود، وأسعده الله فهو مسعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r6.claim: «نؤخره» refers to that Day; al-Hufi instead says it refers to recompense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r6.anchor: وما نؤخره أي: ذلك اليوم. وقيل: يعود على الجزاء قاله الحوفي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r7.claim: The fixed term is a prior decree with a set limit that can neither be advanced nor delayed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r7.anchor: إلا لأجل معدود أي لقضاء سابق قد نفذ فيه بأجل محدود لا يتقدم عليه ولا يتأخر عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r8.speaker: الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r8.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads «يؤخره» with a yāʾ instead of «نؤخره».

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r9.speaker: نافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r9.claim: The two grammarians and Nafiʿ retain the yāʾ of «يأتي» in connected recitation and drop it at pause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r9.anchor: وقرأ النحويان ونافع: يأتي بإثبات الياء وصلا، وحذفها وقفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r10.speaker: ابن كثير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r10.claim: Ibn Kathir retains the yāʾ in both connected and paused recitation; it is also present in Ubayy’s codex.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r10.anchor: وابن كثير بإثباتها وصلا ووقفا، وهي ثابتة في مصحف أبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r11.speaker: باقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r11.claim: The other canonical readers omit the yāʾ in both connection and pause; it is absent from the Uthmanic codex.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r11.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة بحذفها وصلا ووقفا، وسقطت في مصحف الإمام عثمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r12.speaker: الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r12.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads «يأتون»; the same form appears in ʿAbd Allah’s codex.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r12.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش يأتون، وكذا في مصحف عبد الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r13.claim: Abu Hayyan regards retaining the yāʾ in connection and pause as preferable; deletion only at pause follows verse endings, while deletion in both positions eases pronunciation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r13.anchor: وإثباتها وصلا ووقفا هو الوجه، ووجه حذفها في الوقف التشبيه بالفواصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says using the kasra instead of a yāʾ is common in Hudhayl, and cites a line as evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r14.anchor: الاجتزاء بالكسرة عن الياء كثير في لغة هذيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r15.claim: Al-Tabari’s cited poem illustrates the Hudhayli substitution by ending «درهما» with a kasra in place of the yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r15.anchor: كفاك كف ما يليق درهما ... جودا وأخرى تعط بالسيف الدما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r16.claim: The apparent subject of «يأتي» is the Day referred to by «نؤخره» and «ذلك يوم»; «لا تكلم» governs it, meaning no soul speaks that day except by God’s permission, as in another Qurʾanic passage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p209/r16.anchor: والظاهر أن الفاعل بيأتي ضمير يعود على ما عاد عليه الضمير في نؤخره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows the subject of «يأتي» to be God, citing passages about God’s coming and the coming of His command; the yāʾ reading «يؤخره» supports this parse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r1.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن يكون فاعل يأتي ضميرا عائدا على الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r2.claim: He also allows «يوم يأتي» to be governed by an implied “remember,” or by the omitted ending of the fixed term: the term ends when that Day arrives.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r2.anchor: وأجاز أيضا أن ينتصب يوم يأتي باذكر أو بالانتهاء المحذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r3.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r3.claim: Al-Hufi parses «لا تكلم نفس» as a circumstantial clause referring to the Day in «مشهود» or as an adjective of the indefinite «يوم», with «فيه» understood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r3.anchor: وأجاز الحوفي أن يكون لا تكلم حالا من ضمير اليوم المتقدم في مشهود، أو نعتا لأنه نكرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya allows «لا تكلم نفس» as a circumstance of the Day in «يأتي», with «فيه» omitted, or as an adjective of «يوم يأتي»; the latter may mean a time rather than daytime.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: لا تكلم نفس، يصح أن يكون جملة في موضع الحال من الضمير الذي في يأتي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya reconciles other Qurʾanic accounts of speech and argument at the Gathering with this verse by restricting them to God’s permission or to intercession and presenting a proof.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r5.anchor: وما ورد في القرآن من ذكر كلام أهل الموقف في التلازم والتساؤل والتجادل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan says Ibn ʿAtiyya’s parsing of «لا تكلم» appears borrowed from al-Hufi.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r6.anchor: وكلامه في إعراب لا تكلم كأنه منقول من كلام الحوفي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r7.claim: Another view describes Resurrection as a long Day with different stations: people sometimes argue, fall silent without permission, speak by permission, or have sealed mouths while limbs testify.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r7.anchor: وقيل: يوم القيامة يوم طويل له مواقف، ففي بعضها يجادلون عن أنفسهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes «منهم» to mean the people at the Gathering, understood from the no-speech statement and the earlier mention of people gathered.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says «منهم» returns to the collective conveyed by the generic word «نفس».
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: فمنهم عائد على الجميع الذي تضمنه قوله: نفس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas defines the wretched as those whose misery was written and the happy as those whose happiness was written.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الشقي من كتبت عليه الشقاوة، والسعيد الذي كتبت له السعادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r11.claim: Other glosses make the two groups the punished and blessed, or the deprived and provided for.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r11.anchor: وقيل: معذب ومنعم، وقيل: محروم ومرزوق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r12.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210/r12.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the pronoun in «منهم» refers to the community of Muhammad.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan reports al-Hasan’s reading «شقوا» with a ḍamma on the shīn; the majority use a fatḥa.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r4.claim: In the allusive reading, the wretched and blessed are people wholly wretched and wholly blessed.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r4.anchor: يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه فمنهم شقي ) كامل الشقاوة ومنهم سعيد كامل السعادة

TABATABAI:20:108-110/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:108-110/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:108-110/r6.claim: An approved utterance contains no error or sin that angers God; only those purified from mistaken belief, wrongdoing, shirk, and ignorance in this life, or joined to them, can speak acceptably.
TABATABAI:20:108-110/r6.anchor: فمعناه أن لا يخالطه ما يسخط الله من خطأ أو خطيئة قضاء لحق الإطلاق ولا يكون ذلك إلا ممن أخلص الله سريرته

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.claim: The second object can use a clitic pronoun, as in أعطانيه and أعطانيك, when the speaker is placed first.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.anchor: فأما علامة الثاني ~~التي لا تقع إيا موقعها فقولك أعطانيه وأعطانيك فهذا هكذا إذا بدأ المتكلم

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.claim: The order speaker before addressee before absent person governs clitic placement; grammarians' reversed forms are analogical and rejected as unidiomatic.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.anchor: فإن بدأ بالمخاطب قبل نفسه فقال أعطاكني أو بدأ بالغائب قبل نفسه ~~فقال قد أعطاهوني فهو قبيح

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.claim: When the addressee precedes an absent person, the absent object's clitic is acceptable; Sībawayh cites the Qur'anic أنلزمكموها as evidence.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.anchor: وقال عز وجل @QB@ فعميت عليكم ~~أنلزمكموها وأنتم لها كارهون @QE@

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.claim: If both objects refer to absent persons, either clitic order is grammatical, though the separate pronoun form is more common; a poetic line attests the clitic sequence.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.anchor: إذا ذكرت مفعولين ~~كلاهما غائب فقلت أعطاهوها وأعطاهاه جاز وهو عربي

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.claim: With copula-like حسبت and كان, separate إياه forms are usual and fused forms such as حسبتنيه are rare because these verbs relate a subject and predicate rather than perform an action on another.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالمفعولالثانيقدتكونعلامته.anchor: وتقول حسبتك إياه وحسبتني إياه لأن حسبتنيه وحسبتكه قليل في ~~كلامهم وذلك لأن حسبت بمنزلة كان

SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي ونافع
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r1.claim: Abu Amr, al-Kisaʾi, and Nafi retain final yāʾ in connection and drop it at pause; Ibn Kathir retains it in both, while the other canonical readers drop it in both.
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو والكسائي ونافع " يأتي " بإثبات الياء وصلا وحذفها وقفا

SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r2.claim: Ubayy's codex writes the yāʾ and Uthman's omits it; retention is preferred because yāʾ is a root letter, although pause and verse endings omit it.
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r2.anchor: وقد وردت المصاحف بإثباتها وحذفها: ففي مصحف أبي إثباتها، وفي مصحف عثمان حذفها، وإثباتها هو الوجه

SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r3.speaker: الزمخشري وابن جرير
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says Hudhayl often substitutes kasra for final yāʾ; Ibn Jarir cites a poem with تليق and تعط.
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " والاجتزاء بالكسرة عن الياء كثير في لغة هذيل " وأنشد ابن جرير في ذلك:

SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir's cited line كفاك كف ما تليق درهما attests omitting final yāʾ and using kasra instead.
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r4.anchor: 2708 كفاك كف ما تليق درهما جودا وأخرى

SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r5.claim: The preferred governor of يوم is لا تكلم: no soul speaks when that day comes, a good sense requiring no other analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r5.anchor: أحدها: أنه " لا تكلم " والتقدير: لا تكلم نفس يوم يأتي ذلك اليوم. وهذا معنى جيد

SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r6.claim: Other proposed governors for يوم are an omitted اذكر or an implied انتهاء in the omitted phrase إلا لأجل.
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r6.anchor: والثاني: أن ينتصب ب " واذكر " مقدرا. والثالث: أن ينتصب بالانتهاء المحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r7.claim: A fourth proposal supplies another omitted لا تكلم as governor, which the author says is unnecessary.
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r7.anchor: والرابع: أنه منصوب ب " لا تكلم " مقدرا، ولا حاجة إليه

SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r8.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r8.claim: Al-Hawfi treats لا تكلم as a circumstantial clause describing the day in مشهود or as its adjective, with فيه understood.
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r8.anchor: والجملة من قوله: " لا تكلم " في محل نصب على الحال من ضمير اليوم المتقدم في " مشهود "

SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows لا تكلم as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in يأتي, supplying فيه, or as the adjective of يوم يأتي.
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " لا تكلم نفس " يصح أن تكون جملة في موضع الحال من الضمير الذي في " يأتي "

SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r10.claim: The clearer subject of يأتي is the previously mentioned يوم; alternatively, it may be God, as in 2:210 and 6:158.
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r10.anchor: وفاعل " يأتي " فيه وجهان، أظهرهما: أنه ضمير " يوم " المتقدم. والثاني: أنه ضمير الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r11.claim: فمنهم most apparently refers to الناس in مجموع له الناس; al-Zamakhshari and Ibn Atiyya instead take it as the understood people at the gathering, indicated by لا تكلم نفس.
SAMIN-DURR:11:105/r11.anchor: والضمير في قوله: " فمنهم " الظاهر عوده على الناس في قوله:

SAMIN-DURR:11:105#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:105#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:105#2/r1.claim: سعيد has an omitted predicate, ومنهم سعيد, as in the neighboring verse منها قائم وحصيد.

ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r1.speaker: النحويون
ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r1.claim: Grammarians prefer yawm yaʾtī with a written yāʾ, while the codex and reciters have yaʾt with a kasra and no yāʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r1.anchor: الذي يختاره النحويون: يوم يأتي لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه.

ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r2.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r2.claim: The Hudhayl dialect often deletes final yāʾs; Khalil and Sibawayh note forms such as lā adri, where frequent use permits deletion with kasra remaining.
ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r2.anchor: وهذيل تستعمل حذف هذه الياءات كثيرا. وقد ذكر سيبويه والخليل أن العرب تقول لا أدر فتحذف الياء

ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r3.claim: Although writing the yāʾ is grammatically better, Zajjaj prefers the codex reading followed by all reciters, since recitation is transmitted practice and has an Arabic parallel.
ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r3.anchor: والأجود في النحو إثبات الياء والذي أراه اتباع المصحف مع إجماع القراء، لأن القراءة سنة

ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r4.claim: The apparent conflict with other verses saying people do not speak or are questioned is resolved by distinguishing kinds of speech and different scenes of Judgment Day.
ZAJJAJ:v3p77#2/r4.anchor: وهذه الآية فيها سؤال أكثر ما يسأل عنه أهل الإلحاد في الدين

ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r1.claim: No one is asked about sin in order to discover it; God knew their deeds before they performed them.
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r1.anchor: أي لا يسأل ليعلم ذلك منه، لأن الله قد علم أعمالهم قبل أن يعملوها

ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r2.claim: They do speak to confess sins, blame one another, and shift blame, but do not speak an argument that benefits them; thus they can be said not to speak.
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r2.anchor: أي لا ينطقون بحجة تجب لهم، وإنما يتكلمون بالإقرار بذنوبهم ولوم بعضهم بعضا

ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r3.claim: Calling those without a valid argument silent resembles telling a talkative person with empty speech that he has not spoken; disbelievers are likewise deaf and blind because they do not accept or reflect.
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r3.anchor: للذي يخاطبك كثيرا وخطابه فارغ من الحجة: ما تكلمت بشيء

ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r4.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r4.claim: The poet says a person can be deaf to what displeases him while still hearing, illustrating figurative deafness.
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r4.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
أصم عما ساءه سميع

ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r5.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r5.claim: Another view says Judgment Day is long, with stations where speech is forbidden and others where it is permitted; Zajjaj considers both explanations sound.
ZAJJAJ:v3p78/r5.anchor: وقال قوم: ذلك اليوم طويل وله مواضع ومواطن ومواقف

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p339/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p339/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p339/r1.claim: The omitted alif in ولو تر ما أهل مكة is a poetic parallel for deleting the yāʾ in يوم يأت; comparable alif deletion occurs in speech and verse.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p339/r1.anchor: كما حذفت الياء من يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p339/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p339/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p339/r2.claim: Abū ʿUthmān rejects explaining the deletion as a vocative lament: without the lamenting alif, the form would be an ordinary vocative. He treats alif replacing possessive yāʾ as regular, supporting the cited readings.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p339/r2.anchor: قال أبو عثمان: ومن قال ذلك فقد أخطأ

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p339/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p339/r3.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p339/r3.claim: On Abū ʿUthmān’s analysis of alif substituting for possessive yāʾ, Ḥafṣ’s reported reading يا بني throughout the Qurʾān when singular is regular.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p339/r3.anchor: فعلى رأي أبي عثمان يكون ما رواه حفص عن عاصم أنه قرأ في كل القرآن: يا بني إذا كان واحدا

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p373#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p373#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p373#2/r1.claim: These readers pronounce the yāʾ of يأتي in connected reading and omit it at pause; Ibn Kathīr is reported, with some uncertainty, to retain it at pause too. ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥamza omit it in both positions.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p373#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو والكسائي: يوم يأتي بياء في الوصل، ويحذفونها في الوقف

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p373#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p373#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p373#2/r2.claim: The subject of يأتي cannot be the day to which يوم is annexed: that would make the day both the genitive complement of its own verb and that verb’s subject. The subject is not simply the previously mentioned day either.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p373#2/r2.anchor: فلا يجوز أن يكون فاعله ضمير اليوم الذي أضيف إلى يأتي

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p373#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p373#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p373#2/r3.claim: An adverb may be annexed to a clause identified by a separate subject and predicate, but not to a clause identified by its own pronoun; tanwīn can remove the annexation and make the construction possible.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p373#2/r3.anchor: وكذلك لا يجوز أن تضيف الظرف إلى جملة معرفة بضميره

QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#1/r1.claim: Removing hamza from ʾatā produces yātī, smoothing pronunciation without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#1/r1.anchor: Hamza removal — ʾatā loses hamza, becoming yātī; smooths phonetic texture but no semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#2/r1.claim: The waqf variant puts sukūn on the tāʾ when stopping and has no semantic impact.
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#2/r1.anchor: Waqf variant — pausal form with sukūn on tāʾ, standard in stopping

QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#3/r1.claim: The full yaʾtī form restores final yāʾ and removes apocopation, normalizing the verb to the indicative imperfect.
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#3/r1.anchor: Full form with final yāʾ restored — removes the apocopation, normalizing to standard indicative imperfect

QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#4/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#4/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#4/r1.claim: The combined reading has yaʾt in pause and yaʾtī in continuation; both forms are canonical.
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:2#4/r1.anchor: Combined waqf/waṣl reading — yaʾt in pause, yaʾtī in continuation; both canonical

QIRAAT-ER:11:105:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:4#1/r1.claim: Assimilating the tāʾ in lā takallamu creates idghām; the variant adds phonetic heaviness and gravity without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:11:105:4#1/r1.anchor: Assimilation of tāʾ — lā takallamu becomes lā ttakallamu with idghām

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the coming day as the appointed day postponed until its term ends; another view refers the pronoun to recompense and stresses divine coming.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r2.claim: The objection that the day comes on the day of its coming is answered by treating a recurring significant time as an event distinct from the time in which it occurs.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r2.anchor: وأجيب أن كل زمان له شأن يعتبر تجدده كالعيد والنيروز

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r3.claim: The two grammarians and Nafi retain yāʾ in connected reading but drop it at pause; Ibn Kathir retains it in both, while the other seven drop it in both. Alusi prefers retention in both.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r3.anchor: وقرأ النحويان ونافع ( يأتي ) بإثبات الياء وصلا وحذفها وقفا وابن كثير

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r4.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r4.claim: Al-A'mash reads a plural verb, as in Abd Allah's codex, meaning the people or those gathered at the standing-place arrive.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r4.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش يوم يأتون بواو الجمع وكذا في مصحف عبدالله

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r5.claim: The denied speech is speech that can benefit or save them, such as an answer or intercession, rather than every utterance.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r5.anchor: أي لا تتكلم بما ينفع وينجي من جواب أو شفاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r6.claim: The speech clause most likely governs the preceding temporal adverb; alternatives attach it to the deadline or supply a deleted command to remember.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r6.anchor: وهذا الفعل على الأظهر هو الناصب للظرف السابق

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r7.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139/r7.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to distinguish Judgment Day situations in which speech is forbidden from those in which permission is given.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r1.claim: Permission concerns truthful answers, while false excuses may be allowed to expose their falsity, as in the unbelievers' denial of associating partners with God.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r1.anchor: وقد ذكر غير واحد أن المأذون فيه الأجوبة الحقة والممنوع منه الأعذار الباطلة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r2.speaker: السيد المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r2.claim: Al-Murtada notes the apparent tension with verses saying people do not speak or receive permission to excuse themselves, and with their questioning one another.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r3.claim: False utterances may be permitted to expose unbelievers' claims, such as their denial that they associated partners with God.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r4.speaker: قوم من المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r4.claim: Some commentators reconcile the passages by saying the extended Judgment Day includes periods when speech is forbidden and others when it is permitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r4.anchor: وأجاب قوم من المفسرين عن ذلك بأن يوم القيامة يوم طويل ممتد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r5.speaker: السيد المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r5.claim: Al-Murtada understands denied speech as speech that is heard, accepted, and useful for proof or escape; mere blame and questioning do not count.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r5.anchor: والجواب السديد عن ذلك أن يقال

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r6.claim: A poet's image of being deaf to a neighbor's speech illustrates how denial can mean denying effective speech, not every sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r6.anchor: ومثله قول الشاعر : أعمى إذا ما جارتي خرجت

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r7.claim: One explanation says they are not ordered to make excuses because that scene has no legal responsibility and terror forces confession.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r7.anchor: إنهم غير مأمورين بالإعتذار فكيف يعتذرون

ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p139#2/r8.claim: Alusi prefers taking permission to mean their excuses will not be heard or accepted.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r1.claim: Alusi defends the long-day reconciliation: an extended time can include opposite states that need not last its full duration, and al-Hasan's report can distinguish locations.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r1.anchor: لظهور صحة وقوع الزمان الممتد ظرفا للنقيضين فما إذا لم يقتض كل منهما

ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r2.speaker: بعض الفضلاء
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r2.claim: A scholar says the clause describes a particular moment when the day arrives, so it does not deny speech at other times.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r2.anchor: وقال بعض الفضلاء : لا منافاة بين هذه الآية والآيات التي تدل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya offers that other dialogue occurred by permission or that speech here means intercession and proof; Alusi dismisses both proposals.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : لا بد من أحد أمرين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r4.claim: The exception may be connected to all possible causes of speech or disconnected with an understood reference to speaking by one's own power.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r4.anchor: والإستثناء قيل : من أعم الأسباب أي لا تكلم نفس

ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r5.claim: 'Among them' refers to those at Judgment's stations, everyone implicit in the generic 'soul,' or the gathered people; a report restricting them to Muhammad's community is very strange.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p140/r5.anchor: فمنهم أي أهل المواقف المدلول عليه بقوله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r1.claim: The phrase has an omitted repeated 'among them' before 'fortunate,' supplied from the first phrase; the prepositional phrase is fronted and 'wretched' is subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r1.anchor: بتقدير ومنهم سعيد وحذف منهم لدلالة الأول عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r2.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r2.claim: Al-Raghib defines felicity as divine aid enabling a person to attain good, with wretchedness as its opposite.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r2.anchor: معاونة الأمور الآلهية للإنسان على نيل الخير ويضادها الشقاوة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r3.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r3.claim: Al-Bahr explains wretchedness as hardship and misery of life, and felicity as its opposite; al-Qamus gives a similar definition.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r3.anchor: وفسر في البحر الشقاوة بنكد العيش و سوئه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r4.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r4.claim: In religious usage, the wretched are those deserving Hell under the threat, and the felicitous those deserving Paradise under the promise.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r4.anchor: وفسر غير واحد الأول بمن إستحق النار بمقتضى الوعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r5.claim: The wretched are mentioned first because the passage warns and cautions its audience.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p141/r5.anchor: وتقديم الشقي على السعيد لأن المقام مقام الإنذار والتحذير

ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r4.claim: The sequence gathers all souls, divides them into wretched and fortunate, then partitions the groups; al-Sharif al-Qayrawani's poem illustrates the pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r4.anchor: وقد ذكر أن في الآية صيغة الجمع مع التفريق والتقسيم أما الجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r5.claim: Alusi cites the verse's general statement about every soul and the following division as a progression from gathering to classification.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r5.anchor: في الآية صيغة الجمع مع التفريق والتقسيم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r2.claim: Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i report Ibn Umar's account of the Prophet showing two complete, unalterable books listing Paradise and Hell's people; each person's end matches their deeds, so servants should act steadily.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r2.anchor: خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وفي يده كتابان

ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r3.claim: The report that a person's wretchedness or felicity is set in the womb is explained as the angel learning the decree or, interpretively, as disclosure of God's prior knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r3.anchor: وجاء في حديث الشقي من شقي في بطن أمه والسعيد من سعد في بطن أمه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r4.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades hasan a report from Umar: the decree is finished and written, yet each person is made easy for what they were created.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r4.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه قال

ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r5.claim: The past tense expresses certainty; singular forms portray each party as a unit before plural wording reflects entry into the two abodes in successive groups.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r5.anchor: عبر بالماضي إشارة إلى تحقق الوقوع وأتى بالموصول جمعا إيذانا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r6.claim: The phrase yawm yaʾti is read both with the yāʾ affirmed and with it omitted.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r7.claim: No soul speaks on that day except by God's permission.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r8.claim: People divide into those whose misery was decreed beforehand and those whose happiness was decreed beforehand.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r8.anchor: فمنهم من سبقت له الشقاوة ومنهم من سبقت له السعادة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r9.claim: ʿAlī reports the Prophet's teaching that each person is written as blessed or wretched, yet people must work; each is made easy toward the deeds for which they were created.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p199/r9.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه قال: خرجنا على جنازة فبينا نحن بالبقيع إذ خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r3.claim: The coming may be that of requital or the Day itself (with yawm meaning 'when'), or God, as in the cited passages.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r3.anchor: على أن { يوم } بمعنى حين أو الله عز وجل

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r4.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, and Ḥamza read the verb without its final yāʾ, relying on the kasra in its place.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة { يأت } بحذف الياء اجتزاء عنها بالكسر

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r5.claim: No soul speaks what can benefit and save it, whether an answer or an intercession.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r5.anchor: لا تتكلم بما ينفع وينجي من جواب أو شفاعة

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r6.claim: The clause 'no soul speaks' governs the time adverb; alternatively, the adverb depends on an implied 'remember' or on an omitted verb meaning 'at the end.'
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r6.anchor: وهو الناصب للظرف ويحتمل نصبه بإضمار اذكر أو بالانتهاء المحذوف

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r7.claim: The permission is God's, as in 78:38; this may be a different standing from 77:35–36, or only truthful answers are permitted while false excuses are barred.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r7.anchor: أو المأذون فيه هي الجوابات الحقة والممنوع عنه هي الأعذار الباطلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r8.claim: The wretched are destined for Hell under the threat and the happy for Paradise under the promise; 'them' means those at the gathering, inferred from 'no soul speaks' or meaning people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:104-105/r8.anchor: وجبت له النار بمقتضى الوعيد. { وسعيد } وجبت له الجنة بموجب الوعد

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r12.claim: The division into wretched and blessed remains sound: it covers all at the gathering, while both states may coexist in one person in different respects.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r12.anchor: لأن ذلك الشرط حيث التقسيم لانفصال حقيقي أو مانع من الجمع

BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r2.claim: Ibn Amir, Asim, and Hamza omit the yāʾ in yaʾti, relying on the preceding kasra, as is common in the Hudhayl dialect.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r2.anchor: وحذف ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة الياء اجتزاء عنها بالكسرة كما هو فاش في لغة هذيل

BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r3.claim: The omitted yāʾ evokes the terror that silences people for two thirds of the Day; the exception suggests permission to speak in its final third, since exceptions are usually smaller than their whole.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى أن شدة هوله تمنع أهل الموقف الكلام

BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r4.claim: Omitting the second tāʾ in takallamu signals that no soul can utter even a little speech without permission.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r4.anchor: ولو أقل كلام بدلالة حذف التاء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r5.claim: Repeated reference in these verses to permission from the Lord underscores His careful nurture and sound governance.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r5.anchor: أي بإذن ربك المكرر ذكره في هذه الآيات

BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r6.claim: The assembly is divided into the wretched, whose misery was fixed and whose worldly conduct followed it, and the happy, whose fixed felicity shaped their path.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r6.anchor: ثبتت له الشقاوة فيسر في الدنيا لأعمالها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r7.claim: Taʾkhir means moving something away from its direction; ajal is a time set for an event, the lām marks cause, purpose, or wisdom unlike ila, and shaqāʾ is the strength of causes of hardship.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p578#2/r7.anchor: الإذهاب عن جهة الشيء بالإبعاد منه

DURR-FULL:v4p475/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says “the day it comes” refers to that Day.
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله يوم يأت قال ذلك اليوم

DURR-FULL:v4p475/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r3.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says people speak Syriac on Resurrection Day.
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي رضي الله عنه قال: كلام الناس يوم القيامة السريانية

DURR-FULL:v4p475/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r4.speaker: عمر بن ذر
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r4.claim: ʿUmar ibn Dharr reports a codex reading with “they come” and “no creature among them speaks.”
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r4.anchor: عن عمر بن ذر أنه قرأ / يوم يأتون لا تكلم منهم دابة إلا بإذنه /

DURR-FULL:v4p475/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r5.claim: ʿUmar asked whether people act on a settled decree; the Prophet said the pens have run, yet each is made easy for what they were created for. Al-Tirmidhi graded it hasan.
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r5.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال: لما نزلت {فمنهم شقي وسعيد} قلت: يا رسول الله فعلام نعمل على شيء قد فرغ منه

DURR-FULL:v4p475/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas calls the division of people and the messengers’ answer in 5:109 two hidden matters.
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: هاتان من المخبآت قول الله {فمنهم شقي وسعيد} ويوم يجمع الله الرسل

DURR-FULL:v4p475/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the wretched as major sinners from the Muslim community: punishment is temporary, intercession removes them, and the exception covers their time in Hell.
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: هاتان من المخبآت قول الله {فمنهم شقي وسعيد}

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r1.claim: No one speaks in God's presence except by His permission.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله : الا باذنه قال : من يتكلم عنده الا باذنه

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r2.speaker: عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r2.claim: Umar asked whether people act according to a settled decree or an unsettled one; the Prophet answered that the decree is settled and the pens have run, yet each person is facilitated toward his path.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن عمر قال : نزلت فمنهم شقي وسعيد سالت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت يارسول الله علام نعمل على شئ قد فرغ منه

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says people will be gathered on one plain, within the caller's hearing and the eye's reach; the wretched are wretched in the womb, while the happy learn from another's fate.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r3.anchor: عن شقيق بن سلمة قال : سمعت عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه يقول ايها الناس انكم مجموعون في صعيد واحد يسمعكم الداعي وينفذكم البصر

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas calls these categories hidden matters and says grave sinners among the Muslim community may be punished in Hell, then released through believers' intercession and admitted to Paradise; they are called wretched while punished.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2084#2/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : هاتان من المخبيات فمنهم شقي وسعيد فهم قوم من اهل الكبائر من اهل هذه القبلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p163/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p163/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p163/r1.claim: The sentence elaborates on the Day when people are gathered in 11:103: its central point is that people divide into the wretched and fortunate, while the opening prepares by evoking the Day's gravity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p163/r1.anchor: جملة { يوم يأتي لا تكلم نفس } تفصيل لمدلول جملة { ذلك يوم مجموع له الناس }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p163/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p163/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p163/r2.claim: Yawm can mean a moment or time rather than an entire day; the Nabigha uses “day” with “daylight hours,” and Tawba ibn al-Humayyir uses “night” for the hour of departure or return.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p163/r2.anchor: وهو استعمال شائع في الكلام العربي في لفظ ( يوم ) و ( ليلة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p163/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p163/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p163/r3.claim: “It comes” refers to the witnessed Day of 11:103—Resurrection—and means that it occurs and arrives, as in 43:66.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p163/r3.anchor: وضمير ( يأتي ) عائد إلى { يوم مشهود } ( هود : 103 ) وهو يوم القيامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r1.claim: Yawm is an adverb attached to “no soul speaks”; the sentence begins anew with the time expression fronted, meaning no one speaks when the witnessed Day arrives.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r1.anchor: ظرف متعلق بقوله : { لا تكلم نفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r2.claim: The pronoun refers to God, who alone permits speech, as in 78:38; this refutes pagan belief that idols have a right to intercede.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r2.anchor: والمعنى أنه لا يتكلم أحد إلا بإذن من الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r3.claim: Under negation, nafs includes every soul, righteous and sinful, and all speech, including an intercessor's words and a person's argument for themself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r3.anchor: و { نفس } يعم جميع النفوس لوقوعه في سياق النفي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r4.claim: The division into wretched and fortunate details the assembled people of 11:103, with its placement after the parenthetical postponement preserving a carefully arranged discourse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r4.anchor: وهذا التفصيل مفيد تفصيل الناس في قوله : { مجموع له الناس }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r5.claim: Shaqi is an adjective describing someone immersed in wretchedness: a bad, harsh condition that conflicts with the person's nature.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r5.anchor: والشقي : فعيل صفة مشبهة من شقي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r6.claim: Sa'id is the opposite: a person immersed in felicity, enjoying good and pleasant conditions; here one faces punishment and hardship, another bliss and ease.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r6.anchor: والسعيد : ضد الشقي ، وهو المتلبس بالسعادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r7.claim: Wretchedness and felicity have many gradations; this verse summarizes the distinction developed in the following descriptions of the two groups.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p164/r7.anchor: والشقاوة والسعادة من المواهي المقولة بالتشكيك فكلتاهما مراتب كثيرة متفاوتة في قوة الوصف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r5.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة وابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو والكسائي والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r5.claim: The readers differ over retaining the yāʾ of yaʾti in connection and pause: ʿAsim, Ibn ʿAmir, and Hamza omit it in both; Ibn Kathir retains it in both; Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and al-Kisaʾi retain it in connection and omit it at pause, also reported from Ibn Kathir. Ubayy's codex keeps it, the Uthmanic codex omits it, and Ibn Masʿud's codex has yawm yaʾtūn, read by al-Aʿmash.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r5.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة «يوم يأت» بحذف الياء من «يأتي» في الوصل والوقف،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r6.claim: Omission at pause imitates verse endings; retention preserves the original, and omission in connected speech lightens pronunciation, as in lā abāl and lā adri, with al-Tabari's line as evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r6.anchor: ووجه حذفها في الوقف التشبيه بالفواصل، وإثباتها في الوجهين هو الأصل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r7.claim: The clause may be circumstantial to the pronoun in yaʾti referring to dhālika yawm, but not to yawm yaʾti itself; under this parse yawm yaʾti is a subject with fa-minhum as predicate and an omitted fīhi in the clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r7.anchor: لا تكلم نفس يصح أن تكون جملة في موضع الحال من الضمير الذي في «يأتي»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r8.claim: Two other parses are possible: the clause may modify yawm yaʾti as an adjective or serve as its predicate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p206/r8.anchor: ويصح أن يكون قوله: لا تكلم نفس صفة لقوله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207/r1.claim: Dhālika yawm means the day whose preceding night was mentioned; yawm yaʾti means the time or occasion, not daylight specifically, as in sayings by ʿUthman and Abu Bakr using yawm for today.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207/r1.anchor: وقوله: ذلك يوم يراد به اليوم الذي قبله ليلته، وقوله «يوم يأتي» يراد به الحين والوقت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207/r2.claim: This restriction describes the awe, mental disorientation, and terror of Resurrection; other accounts of questions, blame, and dispute either occur by permission or concern intercession or proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207/r2.anchor: ومعنى قوله: لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه وصف المهابة يوم القيامة وذهول العقل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207/r3.claim: The pronoun in fa-minhum returns to all the souls included by nafs, a generic noun used collectively.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p207/r3.anchor: وقوله فمنهم عائد على الجميع الذي تضمنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and al-Kisāʾī pronounce the yāʾ in يوم يأتي when joining; they omit it in pause, except Ibn Kathīr retains it in pause as well.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو والكسائي يوم يأتي بياء في الوصل وحذفوها في الوقف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r2.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r2.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥamza omit the yāʾ both in connection and in pause.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة بغير ياء في الوصل والوقف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says grammarians prefer retaining the yāʾ in يأتي; the written muṣḥaf and most readings have يأت with kasra on tāʾ, a deletion also common in Hudhayl dialect.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج الذي يختاره النحويون يوم يأتي باثبات الياء والذي في المصحف وعليه أكثر القراءات بكسر التاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r4.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r4.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh report that Arabs say لا أدر, dropping the yāʾ and relying on kasra because the expression is frequent; al-Farrāʾ generalizes the deletion to a final silent yāʾ or wāw after a matching vowel and cites poetry.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r4.anchor: وقد حكى الخليل وسيبويه أن العرب تقول لا أدر فتحذف الياء وتجتزئ بالكسرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r5.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r5.claim: The commentators say the Day arrives when all creatures are silent except those God permits to speak; another view takes the statement to concern intercession.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون وقوله ( يوم يأتي ) يعني يأتي ذلك اليوم لا تكلم نفس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says some people have been written down as wretched and others as felicitous.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p158#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس منهم من كتبت عليه الشقاوة ومنهم من كتبت له السعادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350/r5.claim: No one speaks that day except by God’s permission, as also stated in 78:38 and 20:108.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350/r5.anchor: إلا بإذن الله تعالى، كما قال تعالى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350/r6.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350/r6.claim: In the lengthy intercession report in the two Sahih collections, only messengers speak on that day, praying, ‘O God, grant safety.’
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350/r6.anchor: في حديث الشفاعة الطويل: "ولا يتكلم يومئذ إلا الرسل، ودعوى الرسل يومئذ: اللهم سلم سلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350#2/r1.claim: Among those gathered are the wretched and the fortunate, corresponding to the groups in Paradise and the Blaze in 42:7.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350#2/r1.anchor: أي: فمن أهل الجمع شقي ومنهم سعيد، كما قال: {فريق في الجنة وفريق في السعير}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350#2/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350#2/r2.claim: Umar asked whether deeds concern a settled decree or an unfinished matter. The Prophet said the decree and pens had settled it, yet each person is made easy for what they were created to do.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p350#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر، عن عمر (9) رضي الله عنه، قال: لما نزلت {فمنهم شقي وسعيد} سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r2.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r2.claim: Ibn Amir, Asim, and Hamza delete the yāʾ in يأت; other readers retain the original form.
JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r2.anchor: يوم يأت بحذف الياء ابن عامر، وعاصم، وحمزة

JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r3.claim: Deleting the yāʾ lightens the form and relies on kasra; Arabs let kasra stand for yāʾ and ḍamma for wāw, following the written text; Ibn Kathir retains it in both positions.

JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r9.claim: Shiqāʾ is strength of the causes of affliction; related forms mean enduring hardship because one suffers through it.
JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r9.anchor: والشقاء: قوة أسباب البلاء، رجل شقي بين الشقوة والشقوة والشقاوة

JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r10.claim: Saʿāda is strength of the causes of blessing; saʿd means good fortune.
JISHUMI:v5p3561#2/r10.anchor: والسعادة: قوة أسباب النعمة، والسعد: اليمن

JISHUMI:v5p3566/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r1.claim: God knows from the womb who will disobey and be wretched and who will obey and be happy; this does not mean He makes an innocent person wretched without sin, which would invite blame without cause.
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r1.anchor: فالله يعلم أنه شقي، وهو في بطن أمه يعلم أنه يعصي

JISHUMI:v5p3566/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r2.speaker: عمر
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r2.claim: Umar's report says each person is facilitated for what he was created to do; the author takes this as creation for obedience and enablement for it.
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r2.anchor: وما روي في خبر عمر: كل ميسر لما خلق له

JISHUMI:v5p3566/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r3.claim: The author cites the purpose of creation as worship as evidence that people were created for obedience.
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r3.anchor: وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون (56)

JISHUMI:v5p3566/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r4.speaker: رسول الله
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r4.claim: The Prophet's report says every newborn is born upon the natural disposition.
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r4.anchor: وقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: كل مولود يولد على الفطرة

JISHUMI:v5p3569/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r8.claim: Attributing wretchedness and happiness to people shows they act for themselves, refuting the claim that a person is wretched before birth.
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r8.anchor: يدل قوله: شقوا وسعدوا أن الشقاوة والسعادة فعله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r1.claim: The reading omits the yāʾ in ‘yaʾti’; such deletion, with kasra standing in for it, is common in Hudhayl speech, as in ‘lā adri,’ reported by al-Khalīl and Sībawayh.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r1.anchor: قرىء : ( يوم يأت ) بغير ياء . ونحوه قولهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r2.claim: The subject of ‘comes’ may be God, as in 2:210 and 6:158; this is supported by the reading ‘wa-mā yuʾakhkhiruhu’ with yāʾ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r2.anchor: هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله } ( البقرة : 210 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, the subject may be the Day itself, as in 12:107.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الفاعل ضمير اليوم ، كقوله تعالى : { أن تأتيهم * الساعة }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r4.claim: The temporal accusative may attach to ‘no soul speaks,’ an implied ‘remember,’ or the omitted endpoint of the counted term in 11:104.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r4.anchor: إما أن ينتصب بلا تكلم . وإما بإضمار ( اذكر ) وإما بالانتهاء المحذوف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r5.claim: If the Day is the subject, its ‘coming’ means the coming of its terrors and hardships, avoiding the circular claim that the Day comes at its own time.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r6.claim: ‘Lā takallamu’ means ‘does not speak,’ comparable to people speaking only when permitted by the Merciful.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r6.anchor: لا تكلم } لا تتكلم ، وهو نظير قوله : { لا يتكلمون إلا من أذن له الرحمان }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r7.claim: The accounts of people arguing, silence, permitted speech, and limbs testifying describe different scenes during the Day’s long duration.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r7.anchor: ذلك يوم طويل له مواقف ومواطن ، ففي بعضها يجادلون عن أنفسهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r8.claim: The unexpressed antecedent of ‘among them’ is the people of the assembly, implied by ‘no soul speaks’ and mentioned in 11:103.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r8.anchor: الضمير لأهل الموقف ولم يذكروا ؛ لأن ذلك معلوم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r9.claim: The wretched person is bound for Hell because of evil deeds, and the blessed person for the Garden because of good deeds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p404#3/r9.anchor: والشقى الذي وجبت له النار لإساءته ، والسعيد الذي وجبت له الجنة لإحسانه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r1.claim: One explanation is that no one intercedes except by God's permission.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r2.claim: A second explanation is that people can speak only words permitted as good, since they are compelled to leave evil speech.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r2.anchor: لا تتكلم إلا بالمأذون فيه من حسن الكلام لأنهم ملجؤون إلى ترك القبيح

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r3.claim: A third explanation is that at some time during the Resurrection people are barred from speaking without permission.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r3.anchor: لهم في القيامة وقت يمنعون فيه من الكلام إلا بإذنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r4.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r4.claim: Ibn Bahr glosses the two categories as deprived and provided for.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r5.speaker: لبيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r5.claim: Labid's verse glosses them as punished and honored.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r6.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r6.claim: One view says God made people wretched or happy as recompense for their deeds, punishing the disobedient and rewarding the obedient.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r6.anchor: فأسعد المطيع وأشقى العاصي , قاله ابن بحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r7.claim: A second view says God initiated their wretchedness or happiness without it being recompense for deeds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r7.anchor: أن الله ابتدأهما بالشقاوة والسعادة من غير جزاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r8.speaker: عمر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r8.claim: ʿUmar asked the Prophet whether people act according to a settled decree; the Prophet answered that the decree is settled, yet each person is made to follow the path for which they were created.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p503/r8.anchor: روى عبد الله بن عمر عن أبيه أنه قال : لما نزلت

MUQATIL:11:102-105/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:102-105/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:102-105/r5.claim: When that Day comes, no soul speaks except by God's permission; people are divided into wretched and happy.
MUQATIL:11:102-105/r5.anchor: لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه } بإذن الله تعالى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r1.claim: Makkī retains the yāʾ; Abū ʿAmr, Nāfiʿ, and ʿAlī agree in connected reading. Retention is original, while omission for the kasra is common in Hudhayl; the example is 18:64.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r1.anchor: والياء مكى وافقه أبو عمرو ونافع وعلى فى الوصل وإثبات الياء هو الأصل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r2.claim: The subject of yaʾti refers to the day on which all people are gathered, not to the day grammatically annexed to yaʾti; yawm is governed by udhkur or lā takallamu.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r2.anchor: وفاعل يأت ضمير يرجع إلى قوله يوم مجموع له الناس لا اليوم المضاف إلى يأت

NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r3.claim: No one intercedes except by God's permission, as in the verse asking who can intercede with Him except by His leave.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r3.anchor: أى لا يشفع أحد إلا بإذن الله من ذا الذى يشفع عنده إلا بإذنه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r4.claim: The pronoun refers to the people at the gathering, indicated by the preceding statement that no soul speaks and the earlier mention of all people; the wretched are punished and the happy blessed.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p172#2/r4.anchor: الضمير لأهل الموقف لدلالة لا تكلم نفس عليه وقد مر ذكر الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r9.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r9.claim: Al-Qushayrī reports the form without final yāʾ, explaining that yāʾ may be deleted after a preceding kasra, as in lā adrī.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r9.anchor: وقرىء «يوم يأت» لأن الياء تحذف إذا كان قبلها كسرة تقول: لا أدر ذكره القشيري

QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r10.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r10.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr, and al-Kisāʾī retain yāʾ in connected recitation and omit it at a pause.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r10.anchor: قال النحاس: قرأه أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو والكسائي بإثبات الياء في الإدراج، وحذفها في الوقف

QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r11.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r11.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd are reported to read yāti with yāʾ both in connection and at pause.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r11.anchor: وروي أن أبيا وابن مسعود قرأا «يوم يأتي» بالياء في الوقف والوصل

QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r12.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r12.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read yati without yāʾ both in connected reading and at pause.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r12.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وحمزة «يوم يأت» بغير ياء في الوقف والوصل

QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r13.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās prefers retaining yāʾ in connected reading and not pausing here, because grammarians disallow deleting yāʾ without a jussive cause.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r13.anchor: قال أبو جعفر النحاس: الوجه في هذا ألا يوقف عليه، وأن يوصل بالياء، لأن جماعة من النحويين قالوا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r14.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r14.claim: Al-Kisāʾī allows deletion at pause by analogy with pausing on a sound verb as if jussive, dropping yāʾ as one drops ḍamma.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r14.anchor: فأما الوقف بغير ياء ففيه قول للكسائي قال: لأن الفعل السالم يوقف عليه كالمجزوم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r15.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r15.claim: Abū ʿUbayd supports Ḥamza’s deletion in both positions by citing the alleged ʿUthmānic codex spelling and a Hudhayl usage such as mā adr.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r15.anchor: احتج أبو عبيد لحذف الياء في الوصل والوقف بحجتين إحداهما: أنه زعم أنه رآه في الإمام

QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r16.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r16.claim: Al-Naḥḥās rejects Abū ʿUbayd’s codex argument, noting most scholars dispute it and quoting Mālik that the codex was gone; the Hudhayl deletion is old, explained, and not analogically extended.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:102-105/r16.anchor: قال النحاس: أما حجته بمصحف عثمان رضي الله عنه فشيء يرده عليه أكثر العلماء قال مالك بن أنس

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r1.claim: The verse cited by al-Farrāʾ illustrates deleting final yāʾ in taʿṭi, meaning taʿṭī (you give); Sībawayh and al-Khalīl also report lā adrī with yāʾ omitted and the kasra retained through frequent use.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r1.anchor: كفاك كف ما تليق درهما جودا وأخرى تعط بالسيف الدما أي تعطي

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r2.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r2.claim: Sībawayh and al-Khalīl say Arabs use lā adrī with yāʾ omitted and rely on the kasra, allegedly because the form is frequent.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r2.anchor: وقد حكى سيبويه والخليل أن العرب تقول: لا أدر، فتحذف الياء وتجتزىء بالكسرة

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r3.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj considers retaining yāʾ grammatically better and favors following the codex and the readers’ consensus, since recitation is transmitted practice and the form occurs in Arabic.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: والأجود في النحو إثبات الياء قال: والذي أراه اتباع المصحف وإجماع القراء

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r4.claim: Takallamu is originally tatakallamu; one of the two tāʾs is omitted for ease.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r4.anchor: الأصل تتكلم حذفت إحدى التاءين تخفيفا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r5.claim: An implicit “in it” is understood: souls speak only with permission, and the permitted speech is good speech, since they are compelled to abandon evil speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r5.anchor: وفيه إضمار أي لا تتكلم فيه نفس إلا بالمأذون فيه من حسن الكلام لأنهم ملجئون

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r6.claim: Another explanation is that no argument or intercession is spoken without God’s permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r6.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لا تكلم بحجة ولا شفاعة إلا بإذنه

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r7.claim: A further view says there are times during the gathering when people are barred from speaking except by God’s permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن لهم في الموقف وقتا يمنعون فيه من الكلام إلا بإذنه

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r8.claim: The apparent conflict with verses describing speech, questioning, and argument on Judgment Day is resolved by distinguishing futile speech from speech that could serve as a proof for them.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r8.anchor: وهذه الآية أكثر ما يسأل عنها أهل الإلحاد في الدين.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r9.claim: They do speak to confess sins, blame each other, and shift blame; they do not utter a defensible argument, so speech without a useful proof can be called no speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r9.anchor: وأنهم لا ينطقون بحجة تجب لهم وإنما يتكلمون بالإقرار بذنوبهم، ولوم بعضهم بعضا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r10.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r10.claim: Some say the Day is long and has different stations: speech is forbidden at some and allowed at others.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r10.anchor: وقال قوم: ذلك اليوم طويل، وله مواطن ومواقف في بعضها يمنعون من الكلام

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r11.claim: The pronoun refers either to the souls or to the people previously said to be gathered; the wretched and fortunate are those decreed for wretchedness or felicity.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105/r11.anchor: أي من الأنفس، أو من الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r1.claim: Labīd’s verse uses the contrast of a fortunate person taking his share and a wretched person content with his lot, illustrating the terms in the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r1.anchor: فمنهم سعيد آخذ بنصيبه ومنهم شقي بالمعيشة قانع

QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r2.claim: When ʿUmar asked whether people act on a settled decree, the Prophet replied that the matter is already decreed and each person is enabled toward what they were created for; al-Tirmidhī grades this route ḥasan gharīb.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:105-108/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية: { فمنهم شقي وسعيد } سألت رسول الله

QASHANI:11:105-108/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:105-108/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:105-108/r1.claim: The indefinite forms of wretched and blessed are for exaltation and indicate people wretched or blessed from pre-eternity to eternity.
QASHANI:11:105-108/r1.anchor: لما أطلق الشقي والسعيد منكرين للتعظيم دل على الشقي والسعيد الأزليين الأبديين

RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r1.claim: Abu ʿAmr, ʿAsim, and Hamza omit the final ya in yāti; others retain it. Al-Kashshaf says Hudhayl often replaces omitted ya with kasra, as in la adri, cited by al-Khalil and Sibawayh.
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة { يأت } بحذف الياء والباقون بإثبات الياء

RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r2.claim: Al-Kashshaf says God is the subject of ‘comes,’ adducing verses and a variant reading as support.
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r2.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : فاعل يأتي هو الله تعالى كقوله : { هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله }

RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r3.claim: Al-Razi rejects the attribution: the cited verses occur in quoted speech, the first likely from Jews, and do not prove it; although ‘Your Lord came’ is explicit elsewhere, it admits interpretations.
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r3.anchor: لا يعجبني هذا التأويل ، لأن قوله : { حكيم هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله } حكاه الله تعالى عن أقوام

RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi supplies an omitted subject: the day when the terrifying, tremendous thing comes. Suppressing its identification intensifies the warning.
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r4.anchor: بل الواجب أن يقال : المراد منه يوم يأتي الشيء المهيب الهائل المستعظم ، فحذف الله تعالى ذكره بتعيينه

RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r5.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r5.claim: Al-Kashshaf says the adverbial ‘day’ is governed by ‘no soul speaks’ or an implied ‘remember.’
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r5.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : العامل في انتصاب الظرف هو قوله : { لا تكلم } أو إضمار اذكر

RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r6.claim: The wording omits ‘on that day’; the full sense is that no soul speaks on that day except with God’s permission.
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r6.anchor: أما قوله : { لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه } ففيه حذف ، والتقدير : لا تكلم نفس فيه إلا بإذن الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r7.claim: Other verses depict souls arguing, swearing falsely, being halted, or unable to speak or excuse themselves; speech varies by moment in the long Judgment Day, including moments when limbs testify.
RAZI-FULL:v18p48#2/r7.anchor: كيف الجمع بين هذه الآية وبين سائر الآيات التي توهم كونها مناقضة لهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r1.claim: Al-Kashshaf says ‘among them’ refers to the people at the gathering, implicit because they are known and recalled in the preceding mention of all people gathered.
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : الضمير في قوله : { فمنهم } لأهل الموقف ولم يذكر لأنه معلوم

RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r2.claim: The apparent division into wretched and happy concerns those resurrected for reckoning; children and the mentally ill are outside it because they are not held to account.
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r2.anchor: المراد من يحشر ممن أطلق للحساب وهم لا يخرجون عن هذين القسمين

RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r3.claim: Al-Qadi takes the two categories to rule out people of the Heights being neither in Paradise nor Hell; al-Razi replies that they too could be exempt from accounting if rewards equal punishments.
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r3.anchor: احتج القاضي بهذه الآية على فساد ما يقال إن أهل الأعراف لا في الجنة ولا في النار

RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r4.claim: Al-Qadi also argues that everyone at the Judgment must have greater reward or greater punishment; although equality is rationally possible, the verse supposedly excludes it.
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r4.anchor: القاضي استدل بهذه الآية أيضا على أن كل من حضر عرصة القيامة فإنه لا بد وأن يكون ثوابه زائدا

RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r5.claim: Al-Razi says happy and wretched mean those destined for reward and punishment; naming them does not exclude a third category, as verses naming believers and unbelievers do not disprove a neither category.
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r5.anchor: وتخصيص هذين القسمين بالذكر لا يدل على نفي القسم الثالث ، والدليل على ذلك :

RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r6.claim: Because God has judged some happy and others wretched and knows their states, they cannot change categories; otherwise God’s report would be false and His knowledge ignorant.
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r6.anchor: ومن حكم الله عليه بحكم وعلم منه ذلك الأمر امتنع كونه بخلافه ، وإلا لزم أن يصير خبر الله تعالى كذبا

RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r7.speaker: عمر
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r7.claim: Umar reports asking the Prophet whether people work toward something already decreed; the Prophet says the matter is finished, pens dried, destinies flowed, and each is made ready for what they were created.
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r7.anchor: وروي عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه قال : لما نزل قوله تعالى : { فمنهم شقى وسعيد } قلت يا رسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r8.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r8.claim: The Muʿtazila transmit from al-Hasan that people are wretched by their own deeds and happy by their own deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v18p49/r8.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة : نقل عن الحسن أنه قال : فمنهم شقي بعمله وسعيد بعمله

RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r1.claim: Al-Razi answers the Muʿtazilite report: people are indeed wretched or happy through deeds, but those deeds occur by God’s decree and providence, so his proof stands.
RAZI-FULL:v18p50/r1.anchor: لا نزاع أنه إنما شقي بعمله وإنما سعد بعمله ولكن لما كان ذلك العمل حاصلا بقضاء الله وقدره

STUDYQURAN:11:105/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:105/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:105/r1.claim: Speech on the Last Day only by God's permission is also stated in 78:38 and 20:108, with 36:65 as a comparison.
STUDYQURAN:11:105/r1.anchor: That none will be allowed to speak on the Last Day except with God’s Permission is also related in 78:38

STUDYQURAN:11:105/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:105/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:105/r2.claim: The wretched and felicitous refer respectively to the damned and the saved.
STUDYQURAN:11:105/r2.anchor: The terms the wretched and the felicitous refer to the damned and the saved, respectively

STUDYQURAN:11:105/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:105/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:105/r3.claim: These are common terms for the two groups in Islamic writings and have received extensive attention, especially in Sufi literature.
STUDYQURAN:11:105/r3.anchor: these are among the more commonly used terms for these two groups in Islamic texts, and much has been written, especially in Sufi literature

TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r1.speaker: عامة قراء أهل المدينة
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r1.claim: The majority of Medinan reciters read yāʾ in “yawm yaʾtī.”
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ذلك عامة قراء أهل المدينة بإثبات الياء فيها (يوم يأتي لا تكلم نفس)

TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r2.speaker: بعض قراء أهل البصرة وبعض الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r2.claim: Some Basran and Kufan reciters retain the yāʾ in connected recitation but omit it when stopping.
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ذلك بعض قراء أهل البصرة، وبعض الكوفيين بإثبات الياء فيها في الوصل وحذفها في الوقف.

TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r3.speaker: جماعة من أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r3.claim: A group of Kufan reciters omit the yāʾ both in connected recitation and at a pause.
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ذلك جماعة من أهل الكوفة. بحذف الياء في الوصل والوقف

TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers omitting the yāʾ in both positions, following the written codex and a known Hudhayli dialect.
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r4.anchor: والصواب من القراءة في ذلك عندي: {يوم يأت} [هود: 105] بحذف الياء في الوصل والوقف اتباعا لخط المصحف

TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r5.claim: The omitted yāʾ is supported by Hudhayli usage, illustrated by “ma adri ma taqūl” and a poet's lines using yāʾ-less forms.
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r5.anchor: وأنها لغة معروفة لهذيل، تقول: ما أدر ما تقول، ومنه قول الشاعر: [البحر الرجز] كفاك كف ما تليق درهما جودا

TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
