TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r6.claim: “Lā takallamu” stands for “lā tatakallamu,” with one of the two tāʾs omitted because the remaining one signals it.
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: {لا تكلم} [هود: 105] وإنما هي «لا تتكلم» ، فحذف إحدى التاءين اجتزاء بدلالة الباقية منهما عليها.

TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r7.claim: The plural “among them” refers to the souls that cannot speak except by their Lord's permission, though “soul” appeared in the singular.
TAB-FULL:v12p575#2/r7.anchor: وقوله: {فمنهم شقي وسعيد} [هود: 105] يقول: فمن هذه النفوس التي لا تكلم يوم القيامة إلا بإذن ربها، شقي وسعيد، وعاد على النفس

TAB-FULL:v12p578/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p578/r2.speaker: عمر
TAB-FULL:v12p578/r2.claim: When the verse was revealed, ʿUmar asked whether deeds were already determined; the Prophet replied that the decree was complete and each person is enabled for what they were created for.
TAB-FULL:v12p578/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر، عن عمر، قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية {فمنهم شقي وسعيد} [هود: 105] سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقلت: يا نبي الله

TABATABAI:11:100-108/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r1.claim: The final judgment and recompense require humanity to be gathered so that no one is absent; the preceding verses describe questioning those sent and the messengers.
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r1.anchor: وهذا الشأن على هذا النعت لا يتم الا باجتماع من الناس بحيث لا يشذ منهم شاذ

TABATABAI:11:100-108/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r2.claim: The questioning and intermediate reward or punishment in individual graves differ from the final accounting and decisive, everlasting reward of the Resurrection; barzakh questioning completes the record for Judgment Day, while its garden or fire is only a preliminary lodging.
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r2.anchor: فإن الذي يستقبل الإنسان في البرزخ هو المسألة لتكميل صحيفة أعماله ليدخر لفصل القضاء يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:11:105/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105/r1.claim: The subject of yaʾti is the previously mentioned appointed term to which the Resurrection is deferred; on that day no soul speaks except by God’s leave.
TABATABAI:11:105/r1.anchor: فاعل { يأت } ضمير راجع إلى الأجل السابق الذكر أي يوم يأتي الأجل الذي تؤخر القيامة إليه

TABATABAI:11:105/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105/r2.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:11:105/r2.claim: Al-Majmaʿ takes the coming day to mean the Resurrection and requital, with the pronoun referring to them by contextual indication.
TABATABAI:11:105/r2.anchor: وذكر بعضهم كما في المجمع أن المعنى يوم يأتي القيامة والجزاء

TABATABAI:11:105/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105/r3.speaker: صاحب المنار
TABATABAI:11:105/r3.claim: Al-Manar reads the day as an indefinite time in which the specified Day arrives; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this as making a time contain itself, and says the distinction between general and specified days does not help.
TABATABAI:11:105/r3.anchor: وذكر آخرون - كما في تفسير صاحب المنار - أن المعنى في الوقت الذي يجيء فيه ذلك اليوم المعين

TABATABAI:11:105/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105/r4.claim: If day is treated as an event rather than a time, as in the phrase about the Day the Hour rises, its pronoun could refer to the Day without temporal self-containment.
TABATABAI:11:105/r4.anchor: نعم ربما يؤخذ الزمان متحدا بما يقع فيه من الحوادث فيصير حادثا من الحوادث وتلغى ظرفيته

TABATABAI:11:105/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105/r5.claim: The soul is any one of those present at the gathering, and it can speak only with God’s permission.
TABATABAI:11:105/r5.anchor: لا تتكلم نفس ممن حضر إلا بإذن الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:11:105/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105/r6.claim: The doubled tāʾs in the imperfect of the form tafaʿʿul are commonly and regularly reduced to one.
TABATABAI:11:105/r6.anchor: وحذف أحد التائين المجتمعين في المستقبل من باب التفعل شائع قياسي

TABATABAI:11:105/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105/r7.claim: The bāʾ marks accompaniment, so the exception concerns the permitted speech rather than which speaker is excepted.
TABATABAI:11:105/r7.anchor: والباء في قوله { بإذنه } للمصاحبة فالاستثناء في الحقيقة من الكلام لا من المتكلم

TABATABAI:11:105#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#2/r1.claim: The phrase means that a soul says only speech accompanied by God’s permission; worldly people choose what to say whether or not it is legislatively permitted.
TABATABAI:11:105#2/r1.anchor: والمعنى لا تتكلم نفس بشيء من الكلام إلا بالكلام الذي يصاحب إذنه لا كالدنيا

TABATABAI:11:105#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#2/r2.claim: God’s permission governs every event at all times, so this is not exclusive to the Resurrection; it characterizes that Day because its reality becomes manifest there.
TABATABAI:11:105#2/r2.anchor: وقد ذكرت الصفة أعني عدم تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه من خواص يوم القيامة المعرفة له، وليست بمختصة به

TABATABAI:11:105#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#2/r3.claim: Other descriptions of the Resurrection likewise express truths that hold always: nothing is hidden from God, no one has refuge from Him, and all command belongs to Him.
TABATABAI:11:105#2/r3.anchor: ومن المعلوم أنه تعالى لا يخفى عليه شيء دائما، وليس لشيء منه عاصم دائما

TABATABAI:11:105#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#2/r4.claim: The gathering removes the veil from people, making realities and the truth of God’s sole power, sovereignty, and command fully evident; worldly causes lose their supposed independent force.
TABATABAI:11:105#2/r4.anchor: يوم القيامة ظرف يجمع الله فيه العباد ويزيل الستر والحجاب دونهم فيظهر فيه الحقائق ظهورا تاما

TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r1.claim: Because the Day exposes inner secrets, judgment is based on inward states and qualities rather than evidence uncovered through worldly means; what is hidden now becomes manifest.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r1.anchor: وذلك أن الله تعالى يقول فيما يصف هذا اليوم يوم تبلى السرائر الطارق 9 ويقول

TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r2.claim: Ordinary human speech uses socially agreed sequences of sounds to disclose meanings hidden in one person’s mind from other people, who cannot perceive those meanings directly.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r2.anchor: والتكلم الذي نتداوله نحن معاشر الناس فيما بيننا إنما هو باستخدام أصوات مؤلفة تدل بنحو من الوضع والاعتبار

TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r3.claim: If people could directly sense mental meanings, there would be no need to establish languages or speak them.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r3.anchor: لم نحتج إلى وضع اللغات والتكلم بها ولا كان بيننا ما يسمى كلمة أو كلاما

TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r4.claim: Likewise, an entirely solitary human life would have no speech; worldly life combines the seen and unseen, while a wholly manifest afterlife would not need speech except as disclosure of souls to one another.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#2/r4.anchor: وكذا لو كان النوع الإنساني يعيش في حياته الدنيا عيشة انفرادية غير اجتماعية لم يكن من النطق خبر ولا انعقدت له نطفة

TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r1.claim: Since wrongdoers are recognized by their marks and seized by forelocks and feet, no questioning is needed to identify them on the Day of Judgment.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r1.anchor: يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام الرحمن 41

TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r2.claim: Answering the objection from verses where sinners lie, he says people can inspect their own thoughts without speaking, though habitual inner speech or spoken fragments may arise from worldly practice.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r2.anchor: قلت هذا من ظهور الملكات كما أن الإنسان عند التفكير يشاهد خبايا نفسه من غير حاجة إلى أن يخبر نفسه بما يفكر فيه

TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r3.claim: Polytheists and hypocrites may lie because worldly habits appear as traits, but lying cannot deceive God when their insides, records, witnesses, and bodily testimony are exposed; inability to prostrate similarly comes from entrenched arrogance.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r3.anchor: وهؤلاء المشركون والمنافقون لما اعتادوا الكذب في نشأتهم الدنيا، وعاشوا على كذبات الوهم ظهر منهم ذلك يوم يظهر فيه الملكات والعادات النفسانية

TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r4.claim: He compares the revelation of lying dispositions with the parallel case of people who are called to prostrate but cannot do so; the continuation explains that their established arrogance accounts for this inability.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#3/r4.anchor: وهذا نظير دعوتهم يوم القيامة إلى السجود ثم عدم استطاعتهم

TABATABAI:11:105#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#3/r1.claim: The afterlife is a place of requital, not action: once deeds are done, their consequences necessarily attach to their doer, leaving no human choice in the response there.
TABATABAI:11:105#3/r1.anchor: والنشأة الآخرة دار جزاء لا دار عمل فلا خبر هناك عن الاختيار الإنساني وليس هناك إلا الإنسان وعمله

TABATABAI:11:105#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#3/r2.claim: When summoned, people respond compulsorily, unlike in worldly life when they were called to truth and refused.
TABATABAI:11:105#3/r2.anchor: فإذا دعي استجاب اضطرارا، كما قال تعالى يومئذ يتبعون الداعي لا عوج له

TABATABAI:11:105#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#3/r3.claim: Any speech in response to questioning is compelled and matches the exposed record; mouths are sealed and limbs testify, so it is unlike voluntary worldly speech.
TABATABAI:11:105#3/r3.anchor: اليوم نختم على أفواههم وتكلمنا أيديهم وتشهد أرجلهم بما كانوا يكسبون يس 65

TABATABAI:11:105#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#3/r4.claim: There is no valid excuse against a necessary requital for completed deeds; an excuse would matter only where the outcome still involved choice.
TABATABAI:11:105#3/r4.anchor: فإن العذر إنما يكون في الجزاء الذي فيه شوب اختيار ولتحققه إمكان وجود وعدم

TABATABAI:11:105#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#4/r1.claim: Resurrection speech is not chosen disclosure that may be truthful or false; human choice is lifted there, and speech depends on God’s permission and will, as realities become manifest.
TABATABAI:11:105#4/r1.anchor: أن التكلم يومئذ ليس على وتيرة التكلم الدنيوي كشفا اختياريا عما في الضمير بحيث يمكن معه للمتكلم أن يصدق في كلامه أو يكذب

TABATABAI:11:105#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#4/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:11:105#4/r2.claim: Some say only morally good speech is permitted because people are compelled to avoid wrong; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the unsupported restriction, since the afterlife is requital rather than a field of action and even excuses are not evil speech.
TABATABAI:11:105#4/r2.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن معنى قوله { لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه } أنها لا تتكلم فيه إلا بالكلام الحسن

TABATABAI:11:105#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects restricting the verse to intercession as unsupported; if it meant only speech for or about another, the wording should specify that relation as the parallel phrase does.
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r1.anchor: وفيه أن ذلك تقييد من غير شاهد عليه ولو كان المراد ذلك لكان من حق الكلام أن يقال لا تكلم نفس عن نفس أو في نفس إلا بإذنه

TABATABAI:11:105#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r2.claim: Verses that unqualifiedly deny or affirm individuals speaking are reconciled by the permission stated in 78:38.
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r2.anchor: فيه صنفان صنف ينفي التكلم أو يثبته لأفراد الناس من غير استثناء

TABATABAI:11:105#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r3.claim: Verses denying all speech, whether true or false, are reconciled by this verse when permission means that afterlife speech is compelled rather than freely chosen.
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r3.anchor: وصنف ينفي الكلام على أي نعت كان من صدق أو كذب كقوله هذا يوم لا ينطقون

TABATABAI:11:105#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r4.speaker: صاحب المنار
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r4.claim: Al-Manar says the permission clause reconciles verses that absolutely affirm and deny speech; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī objects that it neither distinguishes the two classes nor explains permission in a way that makes the description distinctive of the Day.
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r4.anchor: حيث قال في تفسير الآية ونفي الكلام في ذلك اليوم إلا بإذنه تعالى يفسر لنا الجمع بين الآيات النافية له مطلقا والمثبتة له مطلقا

TABATABAI:11:105#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r5.claim: One proposed answer is that speech is allowed at some stations of the Resurrection and prohibited at others; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this still depends on divine permission and reduces to his account.
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r5.anchor: وقد يجاب عن إشكال التنافي بوجه آخر وهو أن يوم القيامة يشتمل على مواقف قد أذن لهم في الكلام في بعض تلك المواقف

TABATABAI:11:105#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r6.claim: Another answer takes silence to mean absence of speech with a valid argument, though people still confess sins and blame one another.
TABATABAI:11:105#5/r6.anchor: وقد يجاب بأن المراد بعدم التكلم والنطق أنهم لا ينطقون بحجة، وإنما يتكلمون بالأقرار بذنوبهم

TABATABAI:11:105#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#6/r1.claim: Defining silence as lack of useful argument may fit 77:35, but it gives no coherent meaning to this verse’s statement that no soul speaks except by God’s leave.
TABATABAI:11:105#6/r1.anchor: وفيه إنه لو صح فإنما يصح في مثل قوله { هذا يوم لا ينطقون } وأما مثل قوله { يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه } فلا يرجع إلى معنى محصل

TABATABAI:11:105#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#6/r2.speaker: المرتضى
TABATABAI:11:105#6/r2.claim: Al-Alūsī transmits from al-Murtaḍā’s Ghurar wa Durar that the long Resurrection day has periods when speech is barred and periods when it is allowed; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this conflicts with the verse’s apparent scope and repeats the stations problem.
TABATABAI:11:105#6/r2.anchor: وقد يجاب كما نقله الآلوسي عن الغرر والدرر للمرتضى أن يوم القيامة يوم طويل ممتد فيجوز أن يمنعوا النطق في بعضه

TABATABAI:11:105#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#6/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:11:105#6/r3.claim: Some make the exception disconnected: humans cannot speak by their own power, while speech by God’s leave occurs; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī argues that all human acts always depend on God, so the meaningful distinction is between voluntary worldly speech and compelled speech in the afterlife.
TABATABAI:11:105#6/r3.anchor: ان الاستثناء في قوله { لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه } منقطع لا متصل أي لا تتكلم نفس باقتدار من عندها إلا بإذنه تعالى

TABATABAI:11:105#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#6/r4.claim: Happiness is attaining the good that fulfills and pleases a person’s bodily and spiritual powers; misery is losing that good. In technical usage they are possession and privation, while good is broader than happiness.
TABATABAI:11:105#6/r4.anchor: فسعادة كل شيء أن ينال ما لوجوده من الخير الذي يكمل بسببه ويلتذ به فهي في الإنسان

TABATABAI:11:105#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#7/r1.claim: The surface wording does not itself exclude a third class such as believers, unbelievers, and the unexposed or otherwise incapable; children and the insane are examples of the latter.
TABATABAI:11:105#7/r1.anchor: وظاهر قوله تعالى { فمنهم شقي وسعيد } لا تفيد حصر أهل الجمع في الفريقين

TABATABAI:11:105#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#7/r2.claim: The passage concerns everyone gathered on a witnessed Day that ends in Paradise or Fire, so the incapable are not left indefinitely waiting but ultimately join one of the two groups.
TABATABAI:11:105#7/r2.anchor: ولا يدوم عليهم الحال بالإبهام والانتظار فهم بالآخرة ملحقون بإحدى الطائفتين السعداء أو الأشقياء

TABATABAI:11:105#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#7/r3.claim: Thus the context makes the gathered people fall into the two outcomes, as in the other passage where context makes the Paradise and Fire groups exhaustive though the phrase alone does not.
TABATABAI:11:105#7/r3.anchor: ولازم هذا السياق أن ينحصر أهل الجمع في الفريقين السعداء والأشقياء فما منهم إلا سعيد أو شقي

TABATABAI:11:105#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#7/r4.claim: The verse does not explain whether happiness and misery are intrinsic, fixed by an eternal will, or acquired by action; its setting of exhortation indicates that the path to happiness is made accessible.
TABATABAI:11:105#7/r4.anchor: فلا نظر في الآية إلى شيء من ذلك غير أن وقوع الآية في سياق الدعوة إلى الإيمان والعمل الصالح

TABATABAI:11:105#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r1.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī argues that God’s present judgment and knowledge that some will be happy and others wretched make the outcome impossible to reverse, since reversal would make God’s report false and knowledge ignorant.
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r1.anchor: ومن حكم الله عليه بحكم وعلم منه ذلك الأمر امتنع كونه بخلافه

TABATABAI:11:105#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r2.speaker: عمر
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r2.claim: ʿUmar reports asking the Prophet whether people work on something already decreed; the Prophet answers that it is decreed, the pens are dry and fates have run, yet each person is facilitated toward what they were created for.
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r2.anchor: وروي عن عمر أنه قال لما نزل قوله تعالى { فمنهم شقي وسعيد } قلت يا رسول الله فعلى ماذا نعمل

TABATABAI:11:105#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r3.speaker: الحسن
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī reports the Muʿtazilite attribution to al-Ḥasan that people are wretched or happy through their own deeds; Rāzī replies that the deeds themselves occur by divine decree.
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r3.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة روي عن الحسن أنه قال فمنهم شقي بعمله وسعيد بعمله

TABATABAI:11:105#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls Rāzī’s proof a temporal equivocation: a truthful judgment now about a person’s future state does not make that state present now, just as a forecast does not bring its future event into the present.
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r4.anchor: أما الذي سماه دليلا قاطعا فقد غالط فيه بأخذ زمان الحكم زمانا لنتيجته وأثره

TABATABAI:11:105#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r5.claim: The verse reports that people will be happy or wretched on the Resurrection Day, not that they have those states now or eternally; applying Rāzī’s argument consistently would make every future description hold before the Day as well.
TABATABAI:11:105#8/r5.anchor: إن كان حكما بشقاوتهم وسعادتهم كذلك فإنما هو حكم صادر منه في هذا الآن بأنهم كذا وكذا يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:11:100-108#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#4/r1.claim: The cited saying that each person is made ready for what they were created for does not establish the deterministic claim under discussion.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#4/r1.anchor: فلا دلالة لها على ما ذكره أصلا

TABATABAI:11:100-108#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#4/r2.claim: The deterministic argument makes divine decree render acts necessary and compelled, denying human choice and real causal links between acts and misery or felicity; it reduces those links to customary coincidence.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#4/r2.anchor: توجب صيرورته ضروري الثبوت، ويكون الفعل بذلك مجبرا عليه لا اختياريا

TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r1.claim: An act's complete cause includes human will, sound tools, workable material, time and place, and the absence of obstacles; when all are present, the act necessarily occurs.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r1.anchor: فإن للعمل عله تامة يجب بها وجوده

TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r2.claim: An act is necessary relative to its complete cause but remains possible relative to each cause component, including human will; necessity relative to the whole does not turn the human relation into necessity.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r2.anchor: فللعمل إليها نسبة هي نسبة الوجوب، وله إلى كل واحد من أجزاء علته التامة

TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r3.claim: Human action remains voluntary even though a complete cause necessitates it; divine decree is an active attribute drawn from the ordered causal chain, and effects' necessity relative to their causes does not cancel human choice.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r3.anchor: ينتج أن الفعل اختياري للإنسان في عين أنه لا يخلو في وجوده عن علة تامة موجبة له

TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r4.claim: God's knowledge that wood will burn by fire necessitates combustion conditioned on fire, not unconditioned combustion; likewise, knowledge of a chosen act or misery through disbelief entails its occurrence by choice, not independently of it.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#5/r4.anchor: تعلق علمه تعالى مثلا بأن خشبة كذا ستحرق بالنار يوجب وجوب تحقق الاحتراق المقيد بالنار

TABATABAI:11:106-108/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r5.claim: The collective context of the Day of Gathering favors plural wording; the preceding universal negation uses singular indefinite nafs, then the passage returns to the plural for the two groups.
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r5.anchor: ومقتضاها المضي على هيئة الجمع الذين شقوا والذين سعدوا

TABATABAI:11:107-108#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:107-108#6/r4.claim: The author finds no textual evidence for this view and says it seems to assume that misery and happiness are fated without human acquisition or choice, a reading already rejected.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#6/r4.anchor: وفيه إنه لا دليل عليه من جهة اللفظ

TABATABAI:11:108/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108/r4.claim: The context divides all people gathered for Judgment into two groups, and the clauses beginning with أما explain those same exhaustive groups; they cannot mean only selected sinners and former sinners.
TABATABAI:11:108/r4.anchor: مبدوين بأما التفصيلية مسوقان لتفصيل ما أجمل في قوله

TABATABAI:11:108/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108/r5.claim: Recasting the initial division as a special group leaves the general context unexplained and makes the doubled subjects, durations, and exceptions confusing and needlessly complex.
TABATABAI:11:108/r5.anchor: السياق الظاهر في وصف أهل الجمع عامة لا يساعد على إرادة طائفة خاصة منهم

TABATABAI:11:108#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī formulates the extraction view generally: all the gathered divide into Hell's wretched and Paradise's happy, while both exceptions concern sinful monotheists removed from Hell to Paradise; this avoids most earlier objections.
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r1.anchor: يمكن أن يقرر هذا الوجه على وجه التعميم بأن يقال المراد

TABATABAI:11:108#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r4.claim: People God pardons are not arbitrarily excused: pardon rests on a good deed or intercession, making them happy from the outset and included in Paradise's group, not wretches who must be excepted.
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r4.anchor: هم ليسوا بأشقياء حتى يستثنوا بل سعداء داخلون في الجنة من أول

TABATABAI:11:100-108#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#8/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TABATABAI:11:100-108#8/r2.claim: After 11:105 was revealed, ʿUmar asked the Prophet whether deeds concern a matter already decided; the Prophet said it was decided and the pens had flowed, yet each person is facilitated for what they were created for. Al-Tirmidhi graded the report hasan.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#8/r2.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال لما نزلت { فمنهم شقي وسعيد }

TABATABAI:11:100-108#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#8/r3.speaker: عمران بن الحصين
TABATABAI:11:100-108#8/r3.claim: In Sahih al-Bukhari, ʿImran ibn Husayn asks the Prophet what people work toward; he answers that each is facilitated for what they were created for.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#8/r3.anchor: عن عمران بن الحصين قال قلت يا رسول الله فيم يعمل العاملون

TABATABAI:11:100-108#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#8/r4.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:11:100-108#8/r4.claim: At a funeral, the Prophet says everyone's place in Paradise or Hell is written; when asked whether to rely on that, he commands them to work, says each is facilitated for their creation, and recites 92:5.

TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r1.claim: Before an event becomes actual, it remains possible relative to both existence and nonexistence; wood may become ash or not, and semen may become a human if the remaining causes join or may instead be extinguished.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r1.anchor: أن كلا من الحوادث الجارية في هذا العالم من أعيان وآثارها ما لم يلبس لباس التحقق والوجود

TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r2.claim: Once an object becomes actual, its former alternatives cease: actual ash cannot simultaneously be unburned wood, and an actual human cannot remain nonhuman.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r2.anchor: وصار إنسانا فحسب يمتنع غيره ورمادا يمتنع

TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r3.claim: The world can be viewed both as a necessary chain of actual causes and as a field of possibilities and dispositions before outcomes occur.

TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r4.claim: In the possible, not-yet-realized perspective, choice, effort, education, hope and fear, commands, and reward and punishment have their proper place.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#9/r4.anchor: وعليه يقوم ناموس الاختيار، وبه يتقوم السعي والحركات

TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r1.claim: The first perspective is divine decree: events are determined through their causes, but that determination does not cancel their lack of determination in the domain of action and acquisition.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r1.anchor: والوجه الأول هو وجه القضاء الإلهي

TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r2.claim: Determined outcomes under decree do not negate the open-ended conditions that belong to the sphere of invitation, work, and acquisition.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r2.anchor: ولا يبطل تعين الحوادث بحسبه عدم تعينها بحسب ظرف الدعوة والعمل والاكتساب

TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r3.claim: The questioners inferred that a written destination makes deeds irrelevant and removes links between causes and outcomes, so someone destined for Paradise would reach it whether they acted well or badly.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r3.anchor: إذا قضي للإنسان بالجنة تحتم له ذلك سواء عمل أو لم يعمل وسواء عمل صالحا أو اقترف سيئا

TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r4.claim: They also worried that the means themselves were fixed, leaving no room for choice or effort; their questions chiefly reveal the first inference, though the errors are connected.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r4.anchor: وكأن الذي كانوا يشاهدونه في أنفسهم من صفة الاختيار والاستطاعة صرفهم عن الإشارة إلى ثاني التوهمين وإن كان ناشبا على قلوبهم فإنهما متلازمان

TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r5.claim: The Prophet's answer means God makes the path to each person's created end accessible, as expressed by 80:20 and 7:179.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r5.anchor: أي إن كلا من أهل الجنة الذي خلقه الله لها

TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r6.claim: The route to Paradise is faith and piety, and the route to Hell is polytheism and sin; the destination was not decreed apart from its required conduct.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r6.anchor: وسبيل الجنة هو الإيمان والتقوى، وسبيل النار هو الشرك والمعصية

TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r7.claim: The author defers a fuller treatment of divine decree and destiny to a later appropriate passage.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#10/r7.anchor: وسنستوفي البحث في ذلك عندما نضع الكلام في القضاء والقدر فيما يناسبه من الموضع إن شاء الله تعالى

TABATABAI:11:108#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r1.claim: The Prophet answers the question about destiny: each person is facilitated for what they were created for.

TABATABAI:11:108#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r2.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r2.claim: In ʿAli's narration, the Prophet follows this answer with 92:5–10, describing ease toward good for those who give and fear God, and hardship for those who withhold and deny.
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r2.anchor: فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى فسنيسره لليسرى وأما من بخل واستغنى وكذب بالحسنى فنيسره للعسرى

TABATABAI:11:108#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r3.claim: One cannot expect an end without following its path: this world is a place of effort and movement, and a person receives according to what they strive for, as 53:39–41 says.
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r3.anchor: فالمتوقع لإحدى الغايتين من غير طريقه كالطامع في الشبع من غير أكل

TABATABAI:11:108#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r4.claim: Facilitation presupposes a matter that is not necessary or inevitable; otherwise easing the path would have no meaning.
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r4.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن التسهيل إنما يتحقق في أمر لا ضرورة تحتمه ولا وجوب يعينه ويسد باب عدمه

TABATABAI:11:108#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r5.claim: The hadith preserves two aspects of a person's outcome: necessary decree and possible choice through work; divine invitations address the latter aspect.
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r5.anchor: يدل على أن لما يؤول إليه أمر الإنسان من السعادة والشقاء وجهين وجه ضرورة وقضاء حتم لا يتغير

TABATABAI:11:108#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī points to his earlier discussion of free will while interpreting 2:26.
TABATABAI:11:108#5/r6.anchor: وقد تقدم كلام في الجبر والاختيار في تفسير قوله

TABATABAI:11:108#6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r7.claim: Abu Basir reports Abu Jaʿfar's distinction: the exception is stated for Hell's people but, for Paradise's people, the clause is followed by 'an unsevered gift.'
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r7.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله

AKHFASH:v1p388/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p388/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p388/r1.claim: The form is originally تتكلم; the second, weaker tāʾ drops because two tāʾs together are heavy, unlike assimilation in تذكرون.
AKHFASH:v1p388/r1.anchor: ومعناه "تتفعل" فكان الاصل ان تكون "تتكلم" ولكنهم استثقلوا اجتماع التاءين فحذفوا الاخرة

AKHFASH:v1p388/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p388/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p388/r2.claim: A connecting hamza cannot replace the deleted tāʾ here because it occurs in commands and forms meaning فعَل, not in يَفعل or تَفعل.
AKHFASH:v1p388/r2.anchor: فلأن هذه الالف انما تقع في الامر وفي كل فعل معناه

TABRISI:11:105/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105/r1.speaker: يعقوب
TABRISI:11:105/r1.claim: Yaʿqūb reads يؤخره with yāʾ, while the others use nūn; the yāʾ refers to أخذ ربك, whereas nūn begins a new clause, with the same sense.
TABRISI:11:105/r1.anchor: قرأ يعقوب وما يؤخره بالياء والباقون بالنون

TABRISI:11:105/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105/r2.claim: The yāʾ reading refers back to أخذ ربك; the nūn reading begins independently, but has the same meaning.
TABRISI:11:105/r2.anchor: من قرأ يؤخره بالياء فإنه رده إلى قوله أخذ ربك

TABRISI:11:105/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وأهل عرفة غير الكسائي
TABRISI:11:105/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and the readers of ʿArafa except al-Kisāʾī omit the final yāʾ in يأت; the remaining readers retain it.
TABRISI:11:105/r3.anchor: وقرأ يوم يأت بغير ياء ابن عامر وأهل عرفة غير الكسائي

TABRISI:11:105/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105/r4.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:11:105/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj prefers the grammarians’ form يوم يأتي; Hudhayl often delete these yāʾs.
TABRISI:11:105/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: الذي يختاره النحويون يوم يأتي

TABRISI:11:105/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105/r5.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
TABRISI:11:105/r5.claim: Sibawayh and al-Khalīl report that Arabs delete the yāʾ in لا أدر through frequent use.
TABRISI:11:105/r5.anchor: حكى سيبويه والخليل أن العرب تقول لا أدر

TABRISI:11:105/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:11:105/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī says retaining yāʾ in connection and pause is the clear regular form; deletion at pause analogizes it to omitted inflection, while deletion in both positions treats it like established irregular forms.
TABRISI:11:105/r6.anchor: من أثبت الياء في الوصل والوقف فهو القياس البين

TABRISI:11:105/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105/r7.claim: A cited poetic line deletes the yāʾ of تعطي even though nothing requires deletion.

TABRISI:11:104-108/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:104-108/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:104-108/r10.claim: The day cannot be the subject pronoun of يأتي when it is itself governed by that verb; making the day definite through its own pronoun is rejected.
TABRISI:11:104-108/r10.anchor: فلا يجوز أن يكون فاعله ضمير اليوم

TABRISI:11:104-108/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:104-108/r11.speaker: أبو عثمان المازني
TABRISI:11:104-108/r11.claim: A clause definite through a pronoun cannot be annexed to an adverb; adding tanwīn removes the annexation and makes the construction permissible.
TABRISI:11:104-108/r11.anchor: فإن نونت فقلت آتيك يوما ضحوته باردة أو ليلة أولها مطير جاز لأنه خرج بالتنوين عن حد الإضافة وهذا قول أبي عثمان المازني

TABRISI:11:105#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#2/r1.claim: The day that comes is the Day of Judgment already mentioned in 11:103; يوم means a period or span, not daylight.
TABRISI:11:105#2/r1.anchor: أي يوم يأتي هذا اليوم الذي تقدم ذكره لا تكلم نفس

TABRISI:11:105#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#2/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:11:105#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī allows لا تكلم نفس to be a circumstantial clause describing the subject of يأتي or an adjective describing يوم; either analysis requires an understood فيه or deleted object pronoun.
TABRISI:11:105#2/r2.anchor: يجوز أن يكون هذه الجملة حالا من الضمير في يأتي

TABRISI:11:105#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#2/r3.claim: The stronger parse makes يوم يأتي an adverb governed directly by لا تكلم; this avoids the ellipsis required by alternatives, and time nouns naturally attach to verbs.
TABRISI:11:105#2/r3.anchor: وأقول إن الأظهر أن قوله { يوم يأتي } ظرف لقوله

TABRISI:11:105#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#3/r1.claim: لا تكلم means لا تتكلم, with one of the two tāʾs elided, as in the cited poetic example.
TABRISI:11:105#3/r1.anchor: وقوله { لا تكلم } أي لا تتكلم

TABRISI:11:105#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#3/r3.claim: God delays the Day only to a counted term because continued obligation benefits creatures until then; the counted limit signals that the Day is near.

TABRISI:11:105#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#3/r4.claim: The wording لأجل signals a wise purpose for delaying the Day, whereas إلى أجل would not express that purpose.
TABRISI:11:105#3/r4.anchor: وإنما قال { لأجل } ولم يقل إلى أجل

TABRISI:11:105#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#3/r5.claim: The Day’s arrival is the coming of resurrection and recompense.

TABRISI:11:105#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#3/r6.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:11:105#3/r6.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says no one speaks except with God’s permission and command; people are compelled to leave sins, so only permitted good speech occurs.
TABRISI:11:105#3/r6.anchor: فلا يقع منهم فعل القبيح وأما ما هو غير قبيح فإنه مأذون فيه عن الجبائي

TABRISI:11:105#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#3/r7.claim: The more apparent meaning is that no useful speech, such as intercession or mediation, occurs in the Hereafter except by God’s permission.
TABRISI:11:105#3/r7.anchor: والأظهر أن يقال: معناه أنه لا يتكلم أحد في الآخرة

TABRISI:11:105#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#3/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:11:105#3/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan reconciles differing statements by saying the Resurrection has stations: speech is permitted at some and forbidden at others.
TABRISI:11:105#3/r8.anchor: في بعض تلك المواقف ولم يؤذن لهم في الكلام في بعضها عن الحسن

TABRISI:11:105#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#3/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#3/r9.claim: Another explanation takes “no speech” to mean no speech that supplies an argument: sinners may confess, blame one another, and shift guilt, yet such empty talk counts as no speech.
TABRISI:11:105#3/r9.anchor: وقيل: إن معنى قوله { لا ينطقون } أنهم لا ينطقون لحجة

TABRISI:11:105#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#4/r1.claim: Calling people deaf, dumb, and blind explains that argumentless speech counts as no speech: although they hear, speak, and see, they do not accept or consider truth.

TABRISI:11:105#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#4/r2.claim: Not being asked about sin means no inquiry to discover what God already knows; questioning instead serves rebuke, reproach, and proof, as in 37:24.
TABRISI:11:105#4/r2.anchor: فمعناه أنهم لا يسألون عن ذنوبهم للتعرف

TABRISI:11:105#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#4/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#4/r3.claim: People divide into those deserving punishment and reward: the wretched through disobedience, the happy through obedience; misery and happiness are strength of causes of harm and blessing.
TABRISI:11:105#4/r3.anchor: إخبار منه سبحانه بأنهم قسمان أشقياء وهم المستحقون للعقاب

TABRISI:11:105#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#4/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#4/r4.claim: The pronoun منهم may refer to the people gathered on the Day in 11:103, or to نفس in this verse, since نفس is generic.
TABRISI:11:105#4/r4.anchor: يعود إلى الناس في قوله { ذلك يوم مجموع له الناس }

THALABI:v5p188/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p188/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p188/r7.claim: Readers differ over retaining or dropping the yāʾ in yaʾti; both are Arabic forms, and deletion may reflect kasra from yāʾ or ḍamma from wāw.
THALABI:v5p188/r7.anchor: يوم يأت وقرئ بإثبات الياء وحذفه، وهما لغتان وحذف الياء له طريقان

THALABI:v5p188/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p188/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p188/r8.claim: The unnamed poet's line illustrates the deleted-yāʾ form.

THALABI:v5p188/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p188/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p188/r9.claim: No soul speaks on that Day except by God's permission; takallamu is glossed as tatakallamu, like tanazzalu as tatanazzalu.
THALABI:v5p188/r9.anchor: لا تكلم أي: لا تتكلم نفس إلا بإذنه نظير تنزل الملائكة أي: تتنزل

THALABI:v5p188/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p188/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p188/r10.claim: Labid's line illustrates the form taʾajjal, glossed as tataʾajjal.

THALABI:v5p188/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p188/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p188/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says the wretched person is one for whom felicity was written.
THALABI:v5p188/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فمنهم شقي كتبت عليه السعادة

THALABI:v5p188/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p188/r12.speaker: عمر
THALABI:v5p188/r12.claim: Umar asked the Prophet whether deeds were already decreed; the Prophet said the matter was settled and each person is eased toward what they were created for.
THALABI:v5p188/r12.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن عمر، قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v5p188/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p188/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v5p188/r13.claim: A prophetic report says the wretched and fortunate are so from their time in the womb.
THALABI:v5p188/r13.anchor: عليه السلام) : «الشقي من شقي في بطن أمه، والسعيد من سعد في بطن أمه»

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r1.claim: The verb is also read without its final yāʾ; al-Farrāʾ says Arabs omit a quiescent final yāʾ or wāw when the preceding matching vowel suffices, as in the cited poem.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r1.anchor: قال الفراء (¬2): كل ياء أو واو يسكنان وما قبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r2.speaker: الزجاج وسيبويه والخليل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says Hudhayl often deletes these yāʾs; Sibawayh and al-Khalīl also report the dialectal form lā adri without final yāʾ, relying on kasra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬5): هذيل تستعمل حذف هذه الياءات كثيرا، وقد حكى سيبويه والخليل أن العرب تقول: لا أدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī rejects the day in “the day it comes” as the verb's own subject; its subject must be the previously mentioned Day of Gathering.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي (¬6): قوله: {يوم يأت}، فاعل يأتي لا يخلو من أن يكون اليوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī says “day” here means a period or time, not daylight.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p549/r4.anchor: واليوم في قوله: {يوم يأت} هو المراد به الحين والبرهة، ليس (¬5) وضح النهار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r1.claim: One parsing makes “no soul speaks” a circumstantial clause describing the subject of “comes,” with an understood pronoun referring to that day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أن يكون حالا من الذكر الذي في {يأت}، ونقدر فيه ضميرا يرجع إلى ذي الحال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r2.claim: Alternatively, “no soul speaks” describes the day, which is indefinite because it is added to a verb; the sense is that no soul speaks on it, with the locative and pronoun omitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r2.anchor: الضرب الثاني: أن يكون قوله: {لا تكلم نفس} صفة اليوم المضاف إلى {يأت}؛ لأن اليوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r3.claim: Retaining the yāʾ in connected speech is regular; at pause it may be dropped by analogy with verse endings, or retained because it is more substantial than a vowel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r3.anchor: فأما إثبات الياء في الوصل والوقف وإسقاطها؛ فمن أثبتها في الوصل فهو القياس البين؛ لأنه لا شيء يوجب حذف الياء إذا وصل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r4.claim: On the adjectival parsing, deletion of the verb's yāʾ is also possible because an adjective, like a circumstantial clause, can be omitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا أيضا لا يمتنع حذف الياء من في {يأت}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r5.claim: At pause, the yāʾ may be omitted by analogy with an ending, since it resembles a vowel that is dropped at pause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p551/r5.anchor: وأما من حذف في الوقف فلأنها -وإن لم تكن فاصلة- أمكن أن تشبه بالفاصلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p553/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p553/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p553/r1.claim: “Among them” refers to the souls on that Day; “soul” is not restricted to one individual.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p553/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فمنهم} أي من الأنفس في ذلك اليوم؛ لأن النفس في قوله: {لا تكلم نفس}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p553/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p553/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p553/r2.claim: The root of shaqāʾ means hardship and distress; shāqaytu means that two people mutually endured or imposed hardship, as in the cited camel poem.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p553/r2.anchor: وأصل معنى الشقاء في اللغة: الشدة والعسرة يقال: شاقيت فلانا مشاقاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p553/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p553/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p553/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says each person's wretchedness or felicity was decreed for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p553/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬4): {فمنهم شقي} كتبت عليه الشقاوة، {وسعيد} كتبت عليه السعادة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:103-108/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:103-108/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:103-108/r3.claim: No soul speaks on that Day except by God's permission; people are wretched or blessed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:103-108/r3.anchor: { يوم يأت } ذلك اليوم { لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه، فمنهم شقي وسعيد } فمن الأنفس في ذلك اليوم شقي وسعيد.

ELMALILI:11:105/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:105/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:105/r1.claim: On the coming Day, no one will speak without God's permission.
ELMALILI:11:105/r1.anchor: meğer ki O’nun izniyle ola yani Allah’ın izniyle söyleyecek olanlar müstesnâ.

ELMALILI:11:105/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:105/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:105/r2.claim: He cites 78:38, which likewise limits speech to those permitted by the Merciful.
ELMALILI:11:105/r2.anchor: لَّا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ

ELMALILI:11:105/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:105/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:105/r3.claim: Permission does not apply at every station: 77:35–36 describes a station when all are silent and none may speak even to offer an excuse.
ELMALILI:11:105/r3.anchor: هَٰذَا يَوْمُ لَا يَنطِقُونَ وَلَا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ

ELMALILI:11:105/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:105/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:105/r4.claim: Elmalılı identifies those not allowed to speak as wretched and disgraced, while those permitted to speak are fortunate and blissful.
ELMALILI:11:105/r4.anchor: Hiç söyletilmeyenler bedbaht, sefil; söze me’zun olanlar bahtiyar, mes‘uddur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r1.claim: These verses explain the gathering described in 11:103 and portray the Last Day by showing people's outcomes and destinations according to worldly faith and deeds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r1.anchor: Bu âyetler, 103. âyetin “O gün bütün insanların bir araya toplandığı gündür” meâlindeki bölümünü açıklayıcı mahiyette olup

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r2.claim: Because the passage follows stories of idolatrous peoples, one reading takes the warning as directed at people who expect idols to intercede for them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r2.anchor: Âyetlerin, putperest kavimlerin kıssalarının ardından gelmiş olması dikkate alındığında 105. âyetin putların Allah katında kendileri için şefaatçi olacağına inanan kimselere hitap ettiği anlaşılırsa da

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r3.claim: The author prefers a general warning to anyone relying on intercessors instead of avoiding sin: no prophet, saint, angel, or other power can intercede or speak without God's leave.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r3.anchor: o yüce mahkemede Allah’ın izni olmadan ne peygamber ne evliya ne melek ne de başka bir güç şefaat edip söz söyleyebilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r4.claim: People will be divided in the afterlife into the wretched and the happy according to their faith and deeds in this world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r4.anchor: İnsanlar, dünyadaki iman ve amellerine göre âhirette bedbahtlar ve mutlular olmak üzere iki gruba ayrılacaklardır.

BURHAN:v1p53/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p53/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p53/r1.claim: A fāṣila is the word at the end of a verse, like a poetic rhyme or the paired ending of sajʿ; al-Dani instead defines it as the last word of a sentence.
BURHAN:v1p53/r1.anchor: وهى كلمة آخر الآية كقافية الشعر وقرينة السجع وقال الدانى كلمة آخر الجملة

BURHAN:v1p53/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p53/r2.speaker: الجعبرى
BURHAN:v1p53/r2.claim: Al-Jaʿbari says al-Dani's definition departs from the technical usage and lacks support from Sibawayh's examples يوم يأت and ما كنا نبغ, which are not verse endings; reading al-Dani's view through Abu Amr would also entail imāla in من أعطى.
BURHAN:v1p53/r2.anchor: قال الجعبرى وهو خلاف المصطلح ولا دليل له فى تمثيل سيبويه ﴿ يوم يأت ﴾ و ﴿ ما كنا نبغ ﴾

BURHAN:v1p53/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p53/r3.speaker: القاضى أبو بكر
BURHAN:v1p53/r3.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr defines fawasil as similarly shaped ending sounds through which meanings are made clear.
BURHAN:v1p53/r3.anchor: وقال القاضى أبو بكر الفواصل حروف متشاكلة فى المقاطع يقع بها إفهام المعانى

BURHAN:v1p53/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p53/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو الدانى
BURHAN:v1p53/r4.claim: Al-Dani distinguishes fawasil from verse endings: every verse ending is a fāṣila, but a fāṣila may occur elsewhere; speech separated from what follows can be either kind. He cites يوم يأت and ما كنا نبغ as non-endings, unlike إذا يسر.
BURHAN:v1p53/r4.anchor: فالفاصلة تعم النوعين وتجمع الضربين ولأجل كون معنى الفاصلة هذا ذكر سيبويه فى تمثيل القوافى

BURHAN:v1p53/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p53/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p53/r5.claim: Fawasil occur at pauses to beautify the discourse and distinguish Qur'anic speech; they are named for separating one stretch of speech from the next, and the scholars avoid calling them sajʿ.
BURHAN:v1p53/r5.anchor: وتقع الفاصلة عند الاستراحة فى الخطاب لتحسين الكلام بها وهى الطريقة التى يباين القرآن بها سائر الكلام

BURHAN:v1p53/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p53/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p53/r6.claim: Fawasil is preferred to sajʿ because sajʿ derives from a bird's sound and would associate the honored Qur'an with ordinary speech; since Qur'an is God's attribute, it should not receive an unauthorized description even if the meaning were sound.
BURHAN:v1p53/r6.anchor: فشرف القرآن الكريم أن يستعار لشىء فيه لفظ هو أصل فى صوت الطائر ولأجل تشريفه عن مشاركة غيره

BURHAN:v1p53/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p53/r7.speaker: الرمانى
BURHAN:v1p53/r7.claim: Al-Rummani distinguishes sajʿ, whose sound is sought first and bends meaning toward it, from fawasil, which follow meanings and are not ends in themselves; he calls fawasil eloquent and sajʿ defective.
BURHAN:v1p53/r7.anchor: قال الرمانى فى كتاب إعجاز القرآن وبنى عليه أن الفواصل بلاغة والسجع عيب

BURHAN:v1p53/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p53/r8.speaker: القاضى أبو بكر الباقلانى
BURHAN:v1p53/r8.claim: Al-Baqillani adopts al-Rummani's distinction and reports that Ashʿarites deny that the Qur'an contains sajʿ, citing al-Ashʿari's statements in several works.
BURHAN:v1p53/r8.anchor: وتبعه القاضى أبو بكر الباقلانى فى كتاب إعجاز القرآن ونقل عن الأشعرية امتناع كون فى القرآن سجعا

BURHAN:v3p272#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p272#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p272#2/r1.claim: The division into wretched and happy people is an example of the preceding rhetorical device of warning, alongside the examples discussed earlier in the eighth section.
BURHAN:v3p272#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ فمنهم شقي وسعيد ﴾ 8 ونظائره السابقة في الثامن

NAHHAS:v2p302/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p302/r1.claim: The form لا تكلم drops one of the two tāʾs of تتكلم for ease of pronunciation; an anonymous poem is quoted nearby, with no poet identified.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r1.anchor: لا تكلم نفس ) والأصل تتكلم حذفت إحدى التاءين تخفيفا

ITQAN:v3p247#4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p247#4/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p247#4/r1.claim: The passage combines, differentiates, and divides: the indefinite soul under negation generalizes; wretched and happy separate the groups; the following as-for clauses divide them in detail.
ITQAN:v3p247#4/r1.anchor: فالجمع في قوله ﴿ لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه ﴾ لأنها متعددة معنى إذ النكرة في سياق النفي تعم والتفريق

ITQAN:v3p260/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p260/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p260/r1.claim: A fasila is variously defined as a verse's last word, like poetic rhyme or prose assonance; al-Dani instead defines it as a sentence's last word.
ITQAN:v3p260/r1.anchor: الفاصلة كلمة آخر الآية كقافية الشعر وقرينة السجع وقال الداني كلمة آخر الجملة

ITQAN:v3p260/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p260/r2.speaker: الجعبري
ITQAN:v3p260/r2.claim: Al-Jaʿbari rejects al-Dani's definition as contrary to technical usage: Sibawayh's examples are not verse endings, but linguistic rather than technical fasila examples.
ITQAN:v3p260/r2.anchor: الجعبري وهو خلاف المصطلح ولا دليل له

ITQAN:v3p260/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p260/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
ITQAN:v3p260/r3.claim: Qadi Abu Bakr defines fawasil as similarly patterned terminal letters that communicate meanings.
ITQAN:v3p260/r3.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر الفواصل حروف متشاكلة في المقاطع يقع بها إفهام المعاني

ITQAN:v3p260/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p260/r4.speaker: الداني
ITQAN:v3p260/r4.claim: Al-Dani distinguishes a fasila, discourse separated from what follows, from verse heads: every verse head is a fasila, but a fasila need not end a verse.
ITQAN:v3p260/r4.anchor: وفرق الداني بين الفواصل ورؤوس الآي فقال الفاصلة هي الكلام المنفصل عما بعده

ITQAN:v3p260/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p260/r5.speaker: الجعبري
ITQAN:v3p260/r5.claim: Al-Jaʿbari gives two ways to establish verse endings: transmission and analogy. A continuous Prophetic stop proves a fasila and continuous connection excludes one; mixed practice admits several explanations.
ITQAN:v3p260/r5.anchor: وقال الجعبري لمعرفة الفواصل طريقان توقيفي وقياسي أما التوقيفي فما ثبت أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم وقف عليه دائما تحققنا أنه فاصلة

ITQAN:v3p260/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p260/r6.speaker: الجعبري
ITQAN:v3p260/r6.claim: By analogy, an undecided case may be aligned with an explicit one; this adds or removes nothing, but determines division or connection, using prose-sajʿ and poetic rhyme as models.
ITQAN:v3p260/r6.anchor: وأما القياسي فهو ما ألحق من المحتمل غير المنصوص بالمنصوص لمناسب ولا محذور في ذلك لأنه لا زيادة ولا نقصان

ITQAN:v3p260/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p260/r7.speaker: الجعبري
ITQAN:v3p260/r7.claim: Differences in vowel, extension, or tawjih that count as poetic-rhyme defects do not invalidate a Quranic fasila; fasila and prose or rajaz rhyme may shift types, unlike qasida rhyme.
ITQAN:v3p260/r7.anchor: وما يذكر من عيوب القافية من اختلاف الحركة والإشباع والتوجيه فليس بعيب في الفاصلة

ITQAN:v3p260/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p260/r8.speaker: الجعبري
ITQAN:v3p260/r8.claim: Al-Jaʿbari illustrates flexible endings with pairs meaning they return/knowing, the appointment/the reward, and the nightcomer/the piercing star.
ITQAN:v3p260/r8.anchor: ومن ثم ترى ( يرجعون ) مع ( عليم ) ( والميعاد ) مع ( الثواب ) ( والطارق ) مع ( الثاقب )

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r4.speaker: شيخنا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r4.claim: The source’s teacher defines shaqāʾ as the strength of causes of affliction and al-shaqī as the most afflicted person.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r4.anchor: قال شيخنا : الشقاء : قوة أسباب البلاء . والشقي : أعظم أهل البلاء .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r7.claim: The third sense is unbelief: the wretched person is an unbeliever, contrasted with the believer.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r7.anchor: والثالث : الكفر . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة هود

BURHAN:v1p402/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p402/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p402/r2.claim: Zarkashi associates several omitted final yāʾs with matters of the unseen or afterlife; even the ships are considered as signs whose meaning reaches the unseen.
BURHAN:v1p402/r2.anchor: هو داع ملكوتى من عالم الآخرة

DAMGHANI:v1p266/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p266/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p266/r12.claim: Shaqī means an unbeliever, contrasted with the believer in the paired wording.
DAMGHANI:v1p266/r12.anchor: الثاني : الشقي الكافر قوله سبحانه في سورة هود

FARRA:v2p26/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p26/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p26/r10.claim: The word is written without yāʾ although nominative; readers may retain yāʾ in connected recitation or omit it in pause and connection, since a silent yāʾ after kasra is dropped.
FARRA:v2p26/r10.anchor: كتب بغير الياء وهو في موضع رفع، فإن أثبت فيه الياء إذا وصلت القراءة كان صوابا.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r1.claim: The omitted yāʾ in yaʾti signals the Day's nearness: disbelievers repeatedly demand punishment, while the sūra repeatedly promises its soon arrival.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r1.anchor: فأنت ترى أنه تردد استعجال العذاب من ناحية، ومن ناحية أخرى أنه تردد الوعد بقرب حلوله

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r2.claim: After recounting earlier nations' destruction, Hūd says the Judgment will bring the same punishment to unbelievers after only a counted term; the short form signals its swift arrival.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r2.anchor: ثم ذكر أن يوم القيامة آتٍ وأنه سيحل فيه عقاب الكافرين كما حل عقاب الأمم السابقة، وإن هو إلا أجل معدود فيحل

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r3.claim: The author also relates form length to frequency: derivatives of “come” appear 24 times in al-Anʿām and al-Aʿrāf but 13 in Hūd, so Hūd uses the shorter form.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r3.anchor: ذكر الإتيان باشتقاقاته المختلفة في كل من (الأنعام) و (الأعراف) أربعاً وعشرين مرة وفي (هود) تردد ثلاث عشرة مرة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r4.claim: Because speech is restricted to God's permission, the verse drops a yāʾ from yaʾti and one tāʾ from tatakallamu, suggesting little speech on that Day.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#4/r4.anchor: حذف التاء من فعل التكلم فقال: (تَكلَّمُ) ولم يقل: (تتكلم) إشعاراً بقلة الكلام في ذلك الوقت

NASHR:v2p292/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p292/r12.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو والكسائي وابن كثير ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p292/r12.claim: The Medinans, Abu Amr, and al-Kisai retain the yāʾ in connection at يوم يأت; Ibn Kathir and Yaqub retain it in both states, while the others delete it for ease.
NASHR:v2p292/r12.anchor: يوم يأت أثبتها وصلا المدنيان، وأبو عمرو والكسائي، وأثبتها ابن كثير

NASHR:v2p231/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p231/r5.speaker: البزي
NASHR:v2p231/r5.claim: The section lists 31 future verbs whose initial tāʾ may double, across the cited passages; al-Bazzi transmits doubling in the stated routes, including the forms at 20:69 and 49:13.
NASHR:v2p231/r5.anchor: وذلك في إحدى وثلاثين تاء، وهي ولا تيمموا الخبيث هنا،
